title.zh: 卷八十九 南匈奴列傳
title.en: Volume 89: Treatise on the Southern Xiongnu
title.raw: 卷八十九 南匈奴列傳 Volume 89: Treatise on the Southern Xiongnu

sentences.zh: 南匈奴醢落尸逐鞮单于比者，呼韩邪单于之孙，乌珠留若鞮单于之子也。

translations.literal: The Southern Xiongnu Chanyu Bi, titled Huayi Luoshi Zhudi, was grandson of Chanyu Huhanye and son of Chanyu Wuzhuliuruozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Bi—Southern Xiongnu ruler bearing the title Huayi Luoshi Zhudi—was a grandson of Huhanye and son of Wuzhuliuruozhi.

sentences.zh: 自呼韩邪后，诸子以次立，至比季父孝单于舆时，以比为右薁鞬日逐王，部领南边及乌桓。

translations.literal: From after Huhanye, sons succeeded in order; down to Bi's paternal uncle Filial Chanyu Yu's time, Bi was appointed Right Yujian Rizhu Wang, commanding the southern frontier and the Wuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Huhanye's line rotated through the throne, Bi served under his uncle Yu styled Xiaoshanyu as Right Yujian Rizhu Wang, commanding the southern pastures and the Wuhuan.

sentences.zh: 建武初，彭宠反畔于渔阳，单于与共连兵，因复权立卢芳，使入居五原。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, Peng Chong rebelled at Yuyang; the Chanyu with him joined arms, and thereupon again provisionally set up Lu Fang, causing him to enter and dwell in Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianwu, Peng Chong rose in Yuyang; the Chanyu joined him and propped up Lu Fang, who then took up residence in Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 光武初，方平诸夏，未遑外事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangwu, he was just pacifying the Hua domain, had no leisure for foreign affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu was still unifying the interior and could spare no attention for the steppe.

sentences.zh: 至六年，始令归德侯刘飒使匈奴，匈奴亦遣使来献，汉复令中郎将韩统报命，赂遗金币，以通旧好。

translations.literal: By the sixth year, he first ordered Marquis Guide Liu Sa to envoy to the Xiongnu; the Xiongnu also dispatched envoys to come present tribute; Han again ordered Gentlemen-of-the-Palace Han Tong to return the mission, gifting gold coin in order to reopen old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Liu Sa went north as envoy; the Xiongnu reciprocated with tribute. Han Tong carried the reply with gifts of gold to restore former ties.

sentences.zh: 而单于骄踞，自比冒顿，对使者辞语悖慢，帝待之如初。

translations.literal: But the Chanyu sat arrogant, comparing himself to Modun; toward envoys his words were rebellious and rude—the emperor treated him as at first.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu swaggered like Modun and insulted Han envoys; Guangwu bore it without breaking ties.

sentences.zh: 初，使命常通，而匈奴数与卢芳共侵北边。

translations.literal: At first missions constantly connected, but the Xiongnu repeatedly together with Lu Fang jointly invaded the northern border.
translations.idiomatic: Embassies continued while the Xiongnu and Lu Fang repeatedly struck the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 九年，遣大司马吴汉等击之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, dispatched Grand Marshal Wu Han and others to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Guangwu sent Grand Marshal Wu Han against them.

sentences.zh: 经岁无功，而匈奴转盛，抄暴日增。

translations.literal: Passing a year without achievement, yet the Xiongnu turned more flourishing; raiding violence daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign stalled while Xiongnu raids grew bolder.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遂寇河东，州郡不能禁。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, then raided Hedong; provinces and commanderies could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year they overran Hedong; local forces could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 于是渐徙幽、并边人于常山关、居庸关已东，匈奴左部遂复转居塞内。

translations.literal: Thereupon gradually moved You and Bing frontier people east of Changshan Pass and Juyong Pass; the Xiongnu left wing then again shifted to dwell inside the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Han evacuated You and Bing settlers east of Changshan and Juyong; the Xiongnu left wing slipped back inside the wall.

sentences.zh: 朝廷患之，增缘边兵郡数千人，大筑亭候，修烽火。

translations.literal: The court worried over it, increased frontier garrison commanderies by several thousand men, greatly built pavilions and watch-posts, repaired beacon fires.
translations.idiomatic: The court reinforced frontier garrisons by thousands, threw up watchtowers, and relit the beacon chains.

sentences.zh: 匈奴闻汉购求卢芳，贪得财帛，乃遣芳还降，望得其赏。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu heard Han offered reward seeking Lu Fang; greedy to obtain wealth and silk; then sent Fang back to surrender, hoping to obtain that reward.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Han's bounty on Lu Fang, the Xiongnu sent him south to surrender and claim the prize.

sentences.zh: 而芳以自归为功，不称匈奴所遣，单于复耻言其计，故赏遂不行。

translations.literal: But Fang took voluntary return as merit, did not declare Xiongnu sent him; the Chanyu again was ashamed to speak his plot—therefore reward ultimately did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Fang claimed he had defected on his own; the Chanyu shrank from admitting the ruse—no reward was paid.

sentences.zh: 由是大恨，入寇尤深。

translations.literal: From this greatly resentful; invasions especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, they struck deeper into Han territory.

sentences.zh: 二十年，遂至上党、扶风、天水。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, then reached Shangdang, Fufeng, Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year they reached Shangdang, Fufeng, and Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 二十一年冬，复寇上谷、中山，杀略抄掠甚众，北边无复宁岁。

translations.literal: Twenty-first year winter, again raided Shanggu, Zhongshan, killing plundering robbing very many; northern border had no peaceful year again.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they ravaged Shanggu and Zhongshan; the north knew no peace.

sentences.zh: 初，单于弟右谷蠡王伊屠知牙师以次当为左贤王。

translations.literal: At first, the Chanyu's younger brother Right Guli Wang Yitu-Zhiyashi by order ought to become Left Worthy King.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu's brother Yitu-Zhiyashi, Right Guli Wang, stood next in line for the Left Worthy Kingship.

sentences.zh: 左贤王即是单于储副。

translations.literal: Left Worthy King is exactly Chanyu heir-apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Worthy King was heir to the throne.

sentences.zh: 单于欲传其子，遂杀知牙师。

translations.literal: The Chanyu wished to transmit to his son; thereupon killed Zhiyashi.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to crown his own son, the Chanyu murdered Zhiyashi.

sentences.zh: 知牙师者，王昭君之子也。

translations.literal: Zhiyashi—was Wang Zhaojun's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyashi was the son of Wang Zhaojun.

sentences.zh: 昭君字嫱，南郡人也。

translations.literal: Zhaojun's courtesy name was Qiang; she was a Nan commandery person.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang Zhaojun, known as Qiang, came from Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 初，元帝时，以良家子选入掖庭。

translations.literal: At first, in Emperor Yuan's time, as a good-family daughter she was selected into the Ye Court.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuandi she entered the harem as a candidate from a respectable family.

sentences.zh: 时，呼韩邪来朝，帝敕以宫女五人赐之。

translations.literal: At that time Huhanye came to court; the emperor ordered five palace women given him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huhanye visited court, the emperor gave him five ladies-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 昭君入宫数岁，不得见御，积悲怨，乃请掖庭令求行。

translations.literal: Zhaojun entered the palace several years, did not obtain imperial audience, accumulated grief and resentment; then requested the Ye Court director seeking to go.
translations.idiomatic: She languished unseen for years until she begged the harem steward to send her north.

sentences.zh: 呼韩邪临辞大会，帝召五女以示之。

translations.literal: Huhanye on farewell held great assembly; emperor summoned five women to display them.
translations.idiomatic: At Huhanye's farewell audience the emperor presented the five women.

sentences.zh: 昭君丰容靓饰，光明汉宫，顾景裴回，竦动左右。

translations.literal: Zhaojun abundant beauty bright adornment illuminated Han palace; gazing shadow pacing—startling moved left and right.
translations.idiomatic: She appeared radiant among them and stunned every courtier.

sentences.zh: 帝见大惊，意欲留之，而难于失信，遂与匈奴。

translations.literal: Emperor seeing greatly startled, wished to retain her; but found difficulty in breaking faith—thereupon gave her to Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor longed to keep her yet could not break his pledge—so she went to the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 生二子。

translations.literal: Bore two sons.
translations.idiomatic: She bore two sons.

sentences.zh: 及呼韩邪死，其前阏氏子代立，欲妻之，昭君上书求归，成帝敕令从胡俗，遂复为后单于阏氏焉。

translations.literal: When Huhanye died, his former Yanzhi's son replaced the throne, wished to take her as wife; Zhaojun submitted memorial seeking return; Emperor Cheng ordered follow Hu custom; thereupon again became later Chanyu Yanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: After Huhanye died his son by a former wife succeeded and sought her hand per steppe custom; she pleaded to return home but Chengdi commanded her to obey Hu marriage law—she became the next Chanyu's queen.

sentences.zh: 比见知牙师被诛，出怨言曰：“以兄弟言之，右谷蠡王次当立；

translations.literal: Bi seeing Zhiyashi executed, uttered resentful words saying: “Speaking by brothers, Right Guli Wang is next to be established;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhiyashi was executed Bi complained aloud: “Among brothers the Right Guli Wang should succeed;

sentences.zh: 以子言之，我前单于长子，我当立。

translations.literal: Speaking by sons, I former Chanyu's eldest son—I ought to be established.”
translations.idiomatic: and among sons I am the former Chanyu's eldest—I should rule.”

sentences.zh: ”遂内怀猜惧，庭会稀阔。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon inwardly harbored suspicion and fear; court assemblies grew sparse.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he nursed suspicion and avoided court.

sentences.zh: 单于疑之，乃遣两骨都侯监领比所部兵。

translations.literal: The Chanyu suspected him; then dispatched two Gutu marquises to supervise and lead Bi's troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu posted two Gutu marquises to watch Bi's command.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，单于舆死，子左贤王乌达鞮侯立为单于。

translations.literal: Twenty-second year, Chanyu Yu died; son Left Worthy King Wudati Hou established as Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Yu died and his son the Left Worthy King Wudati Hou succeeded.

sentences.zh: 复死，弟左贤王蒲奴立为单于。

translations.literal: Again died; younger brother Left Worthy King Punu established as Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died and his brother Punu, Left Worthy King, took the throne.

sentences.zh: 比不得立，既怀愤恨。

translations.literal: Bi could not be established; already harbored bitter resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Passed over for the throne, Bi burned with resentment.

sentences.zh: 而匈奴中连年旱蝗，赤地数千里，草木尽枯，人畜饥疫，死耗太半。

translations.literal: But within the Xiongnu successive years drought locusts; red earth several thousand li; grass trees all withered; people livestock famine plague—death waste greater half.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year drought and locusts scoured thousands of li bare; famine and plague halved men and herds.

sentences.zh: 单于畏汉乘其敝，乃遣使诣渔阳求和亲。

translations.literal: The Chanyu feared Han would ride their exhaustion; then dispatched envoys to Yuyang seeking marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Han would exploit their weakness, the Chanyu sued for peace through Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 于是遣中郎将李茂报命。

translations.literal: Thereupon dispatched Gentlemen-of-the-Palace Li Mao to return the mission.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent Gentlemen-of-the-Palace Li Mao with the reply.

sentences.zh: 而比密遣汉人郭衡奉匈奴地图，二十三年，诣西河太守求内附。

translations.literal: But Bi secretly dispatched Han man Guo Heng bearing Xiongnu maps; twenty-third year, went to Xihe governor seeking internal attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Bi secretly sent Guo Heng with maps to the Xihe governor in the twenty-third year asking to submit.

sentences.zh: 两骨都侯颇觉其意，会五月龙祠，因白单于，言薁鞬日逐夙来欲为不善，若不诛，且乱国。

translations.literal: The two Gutu marquises somewhat perceived his intent; meeting May dragon sacrifice, therefore reported to Chanyu, saying Yujian Rizhu long has wished to do evil—if not executed, will soon disorder the state.
translations.idiomatic: At the May dragon sacrifice the Gutu marquises warned the Chanyu that Bi meant rebellion and must die.

sentences.zh: 时，比弟渐将王在单于帐下，闻之，驰以报比。

translations.literal: At that time Bi's younger brother Jiangjiang Wang was under Chanyu's tent; hearing it, galloped to report Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's brother Jiangjiang Wang at court galloped west with the warning.

sentences.zh: 比惧，遂敛所主南边八部众四五万人，待两骨都侯还，欲杀之。

translations.literal: Bi feared; then gathered southern eight divisions' masses forty-fifty thousand persons; waited two Gutu marquises return, wished to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Bi rallied forty or fifty thousand men of eight southern tribes and planned to kill the returning Gutu marquises.

sentences.zh: 骨都侯且到，知其谋，皆轻骑亡去，以告单于。

translations.literal: Gutu marquises about to arrive, knew his plot; all light cavalry fled away, to inform Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Forewarned, they fled on fast horses to warn the Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 单于遣万骑击之，见比众盛，不敢进而还。

translations.literal: Chanyu dispatched ten thousand riders to strike them; seeing Bi's masses flourishing, dared not advance and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu sent ten thousand riders but withdrew before Bi's strength.

sentences.zh: 二十四年春，八部大人共议立比为呼韩邪单于，以其大父尝依汉得安，故欲袭其号。

translations.literal: Twenty-fourth year spring, eight divisions' elders together deliberated establishing Bi as Chanyu Huhanye—because his grandfather once relied on Han and obtained peace—therefore wished to inherit his title.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-fourth year eight tribal elders proclaimed Bi Chanyu Huhanye to evoke his grandfather's alliance with Han.

sentences.zh: 于是款五原塞，愿永为籓蔽，扞御北虏。

translations.literal: Thereupon approached Wuyuan barrier, wished forever to be fence screen, ward off northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: They pledged allegiance at Wuyuan and offered to shield Han from the northern Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 帝用五官中郎将耿国议，乃许之。

translations.literal: Emperor adopted Gentlemen-of-the-Palace For All Purposes Geng Guo's proposal; then granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu accepted Gentlemen-of-the-Palace Geng Guo's counsel and approved.

sentences.zh: 其冬，比自立为呼韩邪单于。

translations.literal: That winter, Bi himself established as Chanyu Huhanye.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Bi declared himself Chanyu Huhanye.

sentences.zh: 二十五年春，遣弟左贤王莫将兵万余人击北单于弟薁鞬左贤王，生获之；

translations.literal: Twenty-fifth year spring, dispatched younger brother Left Worthy King Mo leading troops over ten thousand to strike Northern Chanyu's younger brother Yujian Left Worthy King—captured him alive;
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-fifth year Bi's brother Mo led ten thousand men against the Northern Chanyu's brother the Yujian Left Worthy King and took him alive;

sentences.zh: 又破北单于帐下，并得其众，合万余人，马七千匹、牛羊万头。

translations.literal: Again broke Northern Chanyu's tent followers, together obtained their masses—combined over ten thousand persons, horses seven thousand head, cattle sheep ten thousand head.
translations.idiomatic: they smashed the northern court and rounded up more than ten thousand followers with seven thousand horses and myriad cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 北单于震怖，却地千里。

translations.literal: Northern Chanyu trembled in terror; withdrew territory one thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Chanyu recoiled a thousand li in panic.

sentences.zh: 初，帝造战车，可驾数牛，上作楼橹，置于塞上，以拒匈奴。

translations.literal: At first, emperor built war carts, could harness several oxen, above made siege towers, placed on barrier to resist Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu had built ox-drawn tower carts on the frontier against the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 时人见者或相谓曰：“谶言汉九世当却北狄地千里，岂谓此邪？

translations.literal: People of the time seeing perhaps said to each other: “Prophecy says Han ninth generation ought push Di north one thousand li—could it mean this?
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers murmured that the prophecy of Han's ninth reign driving the Di back a thousand li was coming true.

sentences.zh: ”及是，果拓地焉。

translations.literal: ” Reaching this, indeed expanded territory.
translations.idiomatic: Events proved them right.

sentences.zh: 北部薁鞬骨都侯与右骨都侯率众三万余人来归南单于，南单于复遣使诣阙，奉籓称臣，献国珍宝，求使者监护，遣侍子，修旧约。

translations.literal: Northern division Yujian Gutu Marquis together with Right Gutu Marquis led masses over thirty thousand persons to come submit Southern Chanyu; Southern Chanyu again dispatched envoys to palace, offered tribute styled vassal, presented state precious treasures, sought envoy surveillance, dispatched attendant sons, repaired old covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty thousand northerners followed the Yujian and Right Gutu marquises to the Southern Chanyu, who sent tribute and hostages and asked Han supervision under the old treaty.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，遣中郎将段郴、副校尉王郁使南单于，立其庭，去五原西部塞八十里。

translations.literal: Twenty-sixth year, dispatched Gentlemen-of-the-Palace Duan Chen, Vice Colonel Wang Yu to envoy Southern Chanyu, established his court, eighty li from Wuyuan western barrier.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year Duan Chen and Wang Yu invested the Southern Chanyu and fixed his court eighty li inside the western Wuyuan pass.

sentences.zh: 单于乃延迎使者。

translations.literal: Chanyu then extended welcome receiving envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu came forward to greet them.

sentences.zh: 使者曰：“单于当伏拜受诏。

translations.literal: Envoys said: “Chanyu ought prostrate bow receive edict.”
translations.idiomatic: The envoys said he must kneel to receive the edict.

sentences.zh: ”单于顾望有顷，乃伏称臣。

translations.literal: ” Chanyu looked around a moment; then prostrate styled himself subject.
translations.idiomatic: After a pause he knelt and acknowledged Han overlordship.

sentences.zh: 拜讫，令译晓使者曰：“单于新立，诚惭于左右，愿使者众中无相屈折也。

translations.literal: Bow finished; ordered translator inform envoys saying: “Chanyu newly established, truly ashamed before attendants—wish envoys among crowd not mutually bend humiliate.”
translations.idiomatic: When he rose he asked through interpreters that they spare him further public shame.

sentences.zh: ”骨都侯等见，皆泣下。

translations.literal: ” Gutu marquises and others seeing, all wept tears falling.
translations.idiomatic: The Gutu nobles wept at the sight.

sentences.zh: 郴等反命，诏乃听南单于入居云中。

translations.literal: Chen and others returned mission; edict then permitted Southern Chanyu enter dwell Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: They reported back and an edict allowed the Southern Chanyu to settle in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 遣使上书，献骆驼二头，文马十匹。

translations.literal: Dispatched envoys submit memorial, presented camels two head, patterned horses ten horses.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a memorial with two camels and ten fine horses.

sentences.zh: 夏，南单于所获北虏薁鞬左贤王将其众及南部五骨都侯合三万余人畔归，去北庭三百余里，共立薁鞬左贤王为单于。

translations.literal: Summer, Southern Chanyu's captured northern captive Yujian Left Worthy King led his masses together with southern division five Gutu marquises combined over thirty thousand persons rebel-return; removed three hundred li from northern court; together established Yujian Left Worthy King as Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: That summer more than thirty thousand northerners broke away three hundred li from the northern court and raised the captive Yujian Left Worthy King as rival Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 月余日，更相攻击，五骨都侯皆死，左贤王遂自杀，诸骨都侯子各拥兵自守。

translations.literal: Over a month, mutually attacked one another; five Gutu marquises all died; Left Worthy King thereupon committed suicide; various Gutu marquises' sons each held troops self-guarding.
translations.idiomatic: Within weeks they turned on one another—the five Gutu marquises fell, the Left Worthy King killed himself, and each noble's son held his own troops.

sentences.zh: 秋，南单于遣子入侍，奉奏诣阙。

translations.literal: Autumn, Southern Chanyu dispatched son to attend court, presented memorial to palace.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he sent his heir to Luoyang with a memorial.

sentences.zh: 诏赐单于冠带、衣裳、黄金玺、盭緺绶，安车羽盖，华藻驾驷，宝剑弓箭，黑节三，驸马二，黄金、锦绣、缯布万匹，絮万斤，乐器鼓车，棨戟甲兵，饮食什器。

translations.literal: Edict bestowed Chanyu cap belt, robes skirts, gold seal, green twisted cord, peaceful carriage feather canopy, ornate harness four-in-hand, precious sword bow arrows, black bamboo tallies three, side horses two, gold brocade silk cloth ten thousand bolts, floss ten thousand jin, musical instruments drum cart, halberd armor weapons, food drink miscellaneous vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The court showered him with regalia—a gold seal, feather-canopied carriage, arms, ten thousand bolts of silk and brocade, floss, instruments, halberds, and provisions.

sentences.zh: 又转河东米糒二万五千斛。

translations.literal: Again transported Hedong rice dried-rations twenty-five thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-five thousand hu of Hedong grain and army biscuit followed.

sentences.zh: 牛、羊三万六千头，以赡给之。

translations.literal: Cattle sheep thirty-six thousand head—to supply give them.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent thirty-six thousand head of cattle and sheep for subsistence.

sentences.zh: 令中郎将置安集掾史将弛刑五十人，持兵弩随单于所处，参辞讼，察动静。

translations.literal: Ordered Gentlemen-of-the-Palace establish Pacification clerk-scribes leading commuting convicts fifty persons, bearing weapons crossbows following wherever Chanyu dwells, participate lawsuits, observe movements.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen-of-the-Palace posted Pacification clerks with fifty penal troops and crossbows to attend the Chanyu, hear suits, and watch for trouble.

sentences.zh: 单于岁尽辄遣使奉奏，送侍子入朝，中郎将从事一人将领诣阙。

translations.literal: Chanyu year end always dispatched envoys present memorial, send attendant sons enter court; Gentlemen-of-the-Palace attendant clerk one person leads escorts to palace.
translations.idiomatic: Each New Year he forwarded memorials and hostages while a Gentlemen-of-the-Palace clerk escorted them to court.

sentences.zh: 汉遣谒者送前侍子还单于庭，交会道路。

translations.literal: Han dispatched Herald escort former attendant sons return Chanyu court; exchange meet on road.
translations.idiomatic: Han heralds exchanged hostages with Xiongnu envoys along the road.

sentences.zh: 元正朝贺，拜祠陵庙毕，汉乃遣单于使，令谒者将送，赐彩缯千匹，锦四端，金十斤，太宫御食酱及橙、橘、龙眼、荔支；

translations.literal: New Year's court congratulations, worship ancestral temples finished—Han then dispatched Chanyu envoys, ordered Herald lead escort send; bestowed colored silk thousand bolts, brocade four bolts, gold ten jin, palace imperial food sauces and oranges, tangerines, longan, lychee;
translations.idiomatic: After New Year rites Han sent heralds with a thousand bolts of silk, four rolls of brocade, ten jin of gold, imperial preserves, oranges, tangerines, longan, and lychees;

sentences.zh: 赐单于母及诸阏氏、单于子及左右贤王、左右谷蠡王、骨都侯有功善有，缯彩合万匹。

translations.literal: Bestowed Chanyu mother and various Yanzhi, Chanyu sons and Left Right Worthy Kings, Left Right Guli Wangs, Gutu marquises meritorious good—colored silks combined ten thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: the queen mother, consorts, princes, Worthy Kings, Guli Wangs, and deserving Gutu marquises received ten thousand bolts in all.

sentences.zh: 岁以为常。

translations.literal: Year took as constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: This became the yearly routine.

sentences.zh: 匈奴俗，岁有三岁祠，常以正月、五月、九月戊日祭天神。

translations.literal: Xiongnu custom: year has three age sacrifices; always use first fifth ninth month wu day sacrifice Heaven God.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu thrice yearly—in the first, fifth, and ninth months on a wu day—sacrificed to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 南单于既内附，兼祠汉帝，因会诸部议国事，走马及骆驼为乐。

translations.literal: Southern Chanyu already internally attached, also sacrifices Han emperor; thereby convenes various divisions deliberate state affairs; galloping horses and camels for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Chanyu added rites for the Han emperor, convened the tribes on state business, and raced horses and camels for sport.

sentences.zh: 其大臣贵者左贤王，次左谷蠡王，次右贤王，次右谷蠡王，谓之四角；

translations.literal: Their great ministers noble ones: Left Worthy King, next Left Guli Wang, next Right Worthy King, next Right Guli Wang—called four horns;
translations.idiomatic: The chief nobles ranked Left Worthy King, Left Guli Wang, Right Worthy King, Right Guli Wang—the “four horns”;

sentences.zh: 次左右日逐王，次左右温禺鞮王，次左右渐将王，是为六角；

translations.literal: Next Left Right Rizhu Wang, next Left Right Wenjuding Wang, next Left Right Jiangjiang Wang—these are six horns;
translations.idiomatic: then Left and Right Rizhu, Wenjuding, and Jiangjiang kings—the “six horns”;

sentences.zh: 皆单于子弟，次第当为单于者也。

translations.literal: All Chanyu sons younger brothers—by order ought become Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: all royal princes in line for the throne.

sentences.zh: 异姓大臣：左右骨都侯，次左右尸逐骨都侯，其余日逐、且渠、当户诸官号，各以权力优劣、部众多少为高下次第焉。

translations.literal: Different-surname great ministers: Left Right Gutu Marquises, next Left Right Shizhu Gutu Marquises; remainder Rizhu, Juqu, Danghu various official titles—each according power superiority inferiority, division masses many few as high low order.
translations.idiomatic: Non-royal lords included Gutu and Shizhu Gutu marquises; Rizhu, Juqu, and Danghu ranks followed power and following size.

sentences.zh: 单于姓虚连题。

translations.literal: Chanyu surname Xulianti.
translations.idiomatic: The royal clan bore the surname Xulianti.

sentences.zh: 异姓有呼衍氏、须卜氏、丘林氏、兰氏四姓，为国中名族，常与单于婚姻。

translations.literal: Different surnames have Huyan clan, Xubu clan, Qiulin clan, Lan clan four surnames—as state's famous clans, constantly with Chanyu marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The great collateral houses—Huyan, Xubu, Qiulin, Lan—intermarried with the throne.

sentences.zh: 呼衍氏为左，兰氏、须卜氏为右，主断狱听讼，当决轻重，口白单于，无文书簿领焉。

translations.literal: Huyan clan is left; Lan clan, Xubu clan are right—preside break prisons hear lawsuits; ought decide light heavy—mouth report Chanyu; no documents registers.
translations.idiomatic: Huyan headed the left ministers, Lan and Xubu the right; they judged cases orally before the Chanyu without written dockets.

sentences.zh: 冬，前畔五骨都侯子复将其众三千人归南部，北单于使骑追击，悉获其众。

translations.literal: Winter, formerly rebel five Gutu marquises' sons again led their masses three thousand persons return southern division; Northern Chanyu dispatched riders pursue strike—all captured their masses.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, three thousand followers of the rebel Gutu marquises fled south; Northern riders overtook and seized them.

sentences.zh: 南单于遣兵拒之，逆战不利。

translations.literal: Southern Chanyu dispatched troops resist them; opposed battle unlucky.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Chanyu sent troops but lost the engagement.

sentences.zh: 于是复诏单于徙居西河美稷，因使中郎将段郴及副校尉王郁留西河拥护之，为设官府、从事、掾史。

translations.literal: Thereupon again edict Chanyu move dwell Xihe Meiji; thereby Gentlemen-of-the-Palace Duan Chen and Vice Colonel Wang Yu remain Xihe support guard him—for establish official bureaus, attendants, clerk-scribes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then moved the court to Meiji in Xihe; Duan Chen and Wang Yu stayed to staff offices and protect him.

sentences.zh: 令西河长史岁将骑二千、弛刑五百人，助中郎将卫护单于，冬屯夏罢。

translations.literal: Ordered Xihe Chief Clerk yearly lead riders two thousand, commuting convicts five hundred persons, assist Gentlemen-of-the-Palace guard protect Chanyu; winter garrison summer dismiss.
translations.idiomatic: The Xihe chief clerk brought two thousand cavalry and five hundred penal troops each winter to reinforce the escort, standing down in summer.

sentences.zh: 自后以为常，及悉复缘边八郡。

translations.literal: From after took as constant rule; reaching wholly restore frontier eight commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: This became standing practice as Han restored the eight border commanderies.

sentences.zh: 南单于既居西河，亦列置诸部王，助为扞戍。

translations.literal: Southern Chanyu already dwelt Xihe, also arrayed establish various division kings, assist as guard garrison.
translations.idiomatic: From Xihe he posted tribal kings to hold the line for Han.

sentences.zh: 使韩氏骨都侯屯北地，右贤王屯朔方，当于骨都侯屯五原，呼衍骨都侯屯云中，郎氏骨都侯屯定襄，左南将军屯雁门，栗籍骨都侯屯代郡，皆领部众为郡县侦罗耳目。

translations.literal: Made Han clan Gutu Marquis garrison Beidi; Right Worthy King garrison Shuofang; Dangyu Gutu Marquis garrison Wuyuan; Huyan Gutu Marquis garrison Yunzhong; Lang clan Gutu Marquis garrison Dingxiang; Left South General garrison Yanmen; Liji Gutu Marquis garrison Dai commandery—all lead division masses as commanderies counties scout-net eyes ears.
translations.idiomatic: He stationed Gutu marquises and princes at Beidi, Shuofang, Wuyuan, Yunzhong, Dingxiang, Yanmen, and Dai to scout for Han.

sentences.zh: 北单于惶恐，颇还所略汉人，以示善意。

translations.literal: Northern Chanyu fearful; somewhat returned those plundered Han people—to show good intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Chanyu, anxious, began returning captured Han subjects as a gesture.

sentences.zh: 抄兵每到南部下，还过亭候，辄谢曰：“自击亡虏薁鞬日逐耳，非敢犯汉人也。

translations.literal: Raiding troops whenever reached southern division below, returning passed pavilion watch-posts, always apologized saying: “Self-striking fugitive captive Yujian Rizhu only—not dare offend Han people.”
translations.idiomatic: When northern raiders crossed south they apologized at Han posts, claiming they chased only the rebel Rizhu, not Han.

translations.literal: The quotation closes.
translations.idiomatic: They framed every raid as pursuit of Bi's faction alone.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，北单于遂遣使诣武威求和亲，天子召公卿廷议，不决。

translations.literal: Twenty-seventh year, Northern Chanyu then dispatched envoys to Wuwei seeking marriage alliance; Son of Heaven summoned dukes ministers court deliberation—not decided.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year the Northern Chanyu asked for peace through Wuwei; the emperor polled his ministers without resolution.

sentences.zh: 皇太子言曰：“南单于新附，北虏惧于见伐，故倾耳而听，争欲归义耳。

translations.literal: Crown Prince spoke saying: “Southern Chanyu newly attached; northern barbarians fear being attacked—therefore incline ear listening, striving wish submit righteousness only.”
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince argued that the Southern Chanyu had just submitted and the north feared attack—both strained to please Han.

sentences.zh: 今未能出兵，而反交通北虏，臣恐南单于将有二心，北虏降者且不复来矣。

translations.literal: Now unable dispatch troops; yet contrary connect northern barbarians—your servant fears Southern Chanyu will have two minds; northern barbarian surrenderers moreover will not come again.
translations.idiomatic: Parley with the north without troops would alienate the Southern Chanyu and scare off future defectors.

sentences.zh: ”帝然之，告武威太守勿受其使。

translations.literal: ” Emperor approved it; informed Wuwei governor do not receive their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered Wuwei to reject the embassy.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，北匈奴复遣使诣阙，贡马及裘，更乞和亲，并请音乐，又求率西域诸国胡客与俱献见。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, Northern Xiongnu again dispatched envoys to the palace, presenting horses and furs, again begging marriage alliance, and requesting music, also seeking to lead Western Regions states' Hu guests together to come present audience.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 the Northern Xiongnu sent horses, furs, and renewed pleas for marriage ties and court musicians, asking to bring Western Regions allies to audience.

sentences.zh: 帝下三府议酬答之宜。

translations.literal: Emperor sent down to Three Offices deliberation on responding suitably.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the Three Offices how best to answer.

sentences.zh: 司徒掾班彪奏曰：

translations.literal: Minister of Education clerk Ban Biao memorialized saying:
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Ban Biao of the Minister of Education wrote:

sentences.zh: 臣闻孝宣皇帝敕边守尉曰；

translations.literal: Your servant hears Emperor Xiaoxuan instructed frontier guarding commandants saying;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan once told frontier commanders:

sentences.zh: “匈奴大国，多变诈。

translations.literal: “Xiongnu great state, many changes and deceit.
translations.idiomatic: ‘The Xiongnu are a great power and masters of deceit.

sentences.zh: 交接得其情，则却敌折冲；

translations.literal: In dealings obtain their true situation, then repel enemy break shock;
translations.idiomatic: Read them truly and you hold the frontier;

sentences.zh: 应对入其数，则反为轻欺。

translations.literal: Responding fall into their schemes, then instead are lightly deceived.
translations.idiomatic: fall into their schemes and they make a fool of you.’

sentences.zh: ”今北匈奴见南单于来附，惧谋其国，故数乞和亲，又远驱牛、马与汉合市，重遣名王，多所贡献。

translations.literal: ” Now Northern Xiongnu seeing Southern Chanyu come attach, fear plotting their state—therefore repeatedly beg marriage alliance; again from afar drive cattle horses to joint market with Han; heavily dispatch famous kings—much presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Southern Chanyu has submitted, the north fears for its succession—hence marriage bids, livestock markets, and noble embassies heavy with tribute.

sentences.zh: 斯皆外示富强，以相欺诞也。

translations.literal: These all outward display wealth strength—to mutually deceive boast.
translations.idiomatic: It is braggadocio masking exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 臣见其献益重，知其国益虚，归亲愈数，为惧愈多。

translations.literal: Your servant sees their tribute grows heavier—knows their state grows emptier; returning kinship ever more frequent—for fear ever more great.
translations.idiomatic: Heavier gifts betray an emptier treasury; more frequent pleas mean deeper fear.

sentences.zh: 然今既未获助南，则亦不宜绝北，靶縻之义，礼无不答。

translations.literal: Yet now since not yet obtained aiding south, then also not fitting cut off north—bridle-rein meaning—ritual has none not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Han cannot abandon the Southern ally, yet the loose-rein policy toward the north still requires courteous reply.

sentences.zh: 谓可颇加赏赐，略与所献相当，明加晓告以前世呼韩邪、郅支行事。

translations.literal: Deem fitting somewhat increase reward grants, roughly match what they presented—clearly instruct informing about former generations Huhanye, Zhizhi conduct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Increase gifts to match theirs and plainly rehearse the fates of Huhanye and Zhizhi.

sentences.zh: 报答之辞，令必有适，今立稿草并上，曰：“单于不忘汉恩，追念先祖旧约，欲修和亲，以辅身安国，计议甚高，为单于嘉之。

translations.literal: As for the wording of the reply, order that it must be appropriate; now I submit a draft together, saying: “The Chanyu has not forgotten Han’s kindness, recalls the old covenant of his ancestors, wishes to restore marriage alliance, to support himself and secure his state—your plan is most lofty; we commend the Chanyu for it.
translations.idiomatic: The answer must strike the right tone; below is a draft to submit: “You have not forgotten Han’s grace, you recall your forebears’ pact, you seek renewed marriage ties to steady yourself and your realm—your purpose is admirable, and we applaud it.”

sentences.zh: 往者，匈奴数有乖乱，呼韩邪、郅支自相仇隙，并蒙孝宣皇帝垂恩救护，故各遣侍子称籓保塞。

translations.literal: In the past the Xiongnu repeatedly fell into rebellion; Huhanye and Zhizhi bore mutual enmity; both received Emperor Xiaoxuan’s gracious protection—therefore each sent an attendant son, styled himself vassal, and guarded the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the court split: Huhanye and Zhizhi were at odds until Emperor Xuan succored both, so each sent a hostage son and pledged to hold the frontier.

sentences.zh: 其后郅支忿戾，自绝皇泽；

translations.literal: Afterward Zhizhi turned resentful and violent and cut himself off from imperial favor;
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi then turned hostile and broke with the throne;

sentences.zh: 而呼韩附亲，忠孝弥著。

translations.literal: whereas Huhanye cleaved to kinship, and loyalty and filial duty shone all the brighter.
translations.idiomatic: while Huhanye stayed close to us, his loyalty plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 及汉灭郅支，遂保国传嗣，子孙相继。

translations.literal: When Han destroyed Zhizhi, [Huhanye’s branch] was then able to preserve its state, pass on the succession, and sons and grandsons succeeded one another.
translations.idiomatic: Once Han destroyed Zhizhi, Huhanye’s line held its realm and passed the throne from father to son.

sentences.zh: 今南单于携众南向，款塞归命。

translations.literal: Now the Southern Chanyu has led his people southward, knocked at the passes, and submitted to authority.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Southern Chanyu has brought his hosts south to the frontier and offered submission.

sentences.zh: 自以呼韩嫡长，次第当立，而侵夺失职，猜疑相背，数请兵将，归扫北庭，策谋纷纭，无所不至。

translations.literal: He considers himself Huhanye’s legitimate eldest and by order ought to rule, yet suffered seizure of title and loss of position; mutual suspicion and betrayal followed; he has repeatedly asked for troops and generals to return and sweep the Northern Court—plots and schemes proliferate, nothing is left untried.
translations.idiomatic: He claims primacy as Huhanye’s heir yet was ousted; suspicion bred revolt, and he has again and again asked us for arms to retake the northern court—his designs run in every direction.

sentences.zh: 惟念斯言不可独听，又以北单于比年贡献，欲修和亲，故拒而未许，将以成单于忠孝之义。

translations.literal: Only, reflecting that these words cannot be heeded alone, and that the Northern Chanyu in recent years has sent tribute and seeks marriage alliance, therefore we have declined him without granting—intending thereby to fulfill the Chanyu’s meaning of loyalty and filial duty.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot take his word alone; the northern ruler still sends tribute and asks for peace, so we have held him at arm’s length—both to honor his plea for loyalty and to avoid rash promises.

sentences.zh: 汉秉威信，总率万国，日月所照，皆为臣妾。

translations.literal: Han wields awe and trust, leads the myriad states; wherever sun and moon shine, all are servants and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Han commands respect and unites the realm; every land the sun and moon touch owes allegiance.

sentences.zh: 殊俗百蛮，义无亲疏，服顺者褒赏，畔逆者诛罚，善恶之效，呼韩、郅支是也。

translations.literal: Among alien customs and the hundred barbarians, right makes no distinction of near or far: those who submit are praised and rewarded; those who rebel are executed and punished—the outcome of good and evil is Huhanye and Zhizhi.
translations.idiomatic: For every foreign people, duty knows no favorites: reward the obedient, punish rebels—the lesson is written in Huhanye and Zhizhi.

sentences.zh: 今单于欲修和亲，款诚已达，何嫌而欲率西域诸国俱来献见？

translations.literal: Now the Chanyu wishes to restore marriage alliance; his sincerity has already been conveyed—what suspicion remains that he should wish to lead the Western Regions states all together to come present audience?
translations.idiomatic: You ask again for kinship by marriage and have shown good faith—why, then, insist on dragging every Western Regions state to court?

sentences.zh: 西域国属匈奴，与属汉何异？

translations.literal: The Western Regions states belong to the Xiongnu—how do they differ from belonging to Han?
translations.idiomatic: Those kingdoms owe allegiance to you: what changes if they also acknowledge us?

sentences.zh: 单于数连兵乱，国内虚耗，贡物裁以通礼，何必献马裘？

translations.literal: The Chanyu has repeatedly linked arms in turmoil; within the state emptiness and waste—tribute goods are trimmed merely to meet ritual—why must you present horses and furs?
translations.idiomatic: Years of war have drained your realm; protocol gifts should suffice—why send horses and pelts as well?

sentences.zh: 今赍杂缯五百匹，弓鞬韥丸一，矢四发，遣遗单于。

translations.literal: Now we send assorted silks five hundred bolts, one set of bow case, quiver, and pellet pouch, and four bundles of arrows—we dispatch them as gifts to the Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: We send five hundred bolts of mixed silk, a bow case and quiver, and four sheaves of arrows as your gifts.

sentences.zh: 又赐献马左骨都侯、右谷蠡王杂缯各四百匹，斩马剑各一。

translations.literal: Also we grant to the horse-presenting Left Gudu Marquis and the Right Guyuli King assorted silks four hundred bolts each, and to each one horse-slaughtering sword.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Gudu Marquis and Right Guyuli King who brought horses receive four hundred bolts of silk apiece and a sword each.

sentences.zh: 单于前言先帝时所赐呼韩邪竽、瑟、空侯皆败，愿复栽赐。

translations.literal: The Chanyu earlier stated that the yu, se, and konghou granted Huhanye in the former emperor’s time were all ruined; he wishes again to be granted replacement.
translations.idiomatic: You wrote that the mouth-organs, zithers, and lutes given Huhanye under the late emperor are worn out and asked for new ones.

sentences.zh: 念单于国尚未安，方厉武节，以战攻为务，竽瑟之用，不如良弓利剑，故未以赍。

translations.literal: Considering the Chanyu’s state is not yet secure, you are just now enforcing martial discipline and take battle and attack as your task—the use of mouth-organs and zithers is not like good bows and sharp swords—therefore we have not yet sent them along.
translations.idiomatic: Your realm is still unsettled and you live by the sword; strings cannot match steel—so we have not sent instruments.

sentences.zh: 朕不爱小物，于单于使宜所欲，遣驿以闻。

translations.literal: We do not begrudge small things; as for what suits the Chanyu’s envoys’ desires, dispatch relay riders to inform us.
translations.idiomatic: We stint nothing petty; tell us through the post stations whatever else your envoys require.”

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark of Ban Biao’s draft reply.
translations.idiomatic: End of the proposed letter.

sentences.zh: 帝悉纳从之。

translations.literal: Emperor entirely adopted and followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted Ban’s advice in full.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，赐南单于羊数万头。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, granted Southern Chanyu sheep numbering tens of thousands of head.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 the court gave the Southern Chanyu tens of thousands of sheep.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，北匈奴复遣使如前，乃玺书报答，赐以彩缯，不遣使者。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, Northern Xiongnu again dispatched envoys as before—thereupon [the emperor] used imperial-seal letter to reply, granted colored silks, did not dispatch envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In year 31 the north sent envoys again; the throne answered by sealed edict and silk gifts without reciprocating an embassy.

sentences.zh: 单于比立九年薨，中郎将段郴将兵赴吊，祭以酒米，分兵卫护之。

translations.literal: Chanyu Bi, having ruled nine years, died; Commandant of the Gentlemen of the Household Duan Chen led troops to attend mourning, sacrificed with wine and grain, divided troops to guard and protect.
translations.idiomatic: Bi ruled nine years before he died; Colonel Duan Chen brought troops to mourn, offered wine and grain, and detached forces to secure the camp.

sentences.zh: 比弟左贤王莫立，帝遣使者赍玺书镇慰，拜授玺绶，遗冠帻，绛单衣三袭，童子佩刀、绲带各一，又赐缯彩四千匹，令赏赐诸王、骨都侯已下。

translations.literal: Bi’s younger brother Left Wise King Mo succeeded; emperor dispatched envoys bearing imperial-seal letter to pacify and console, invested and handed seal-cords, presented headcloth caps, three suits of crimson unlined robes, for youths paired swords and woven belts one each; also granted silk colors four thousand bolts, ordering reward grants to various kings and Gudu marquises downward.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Mo, the Left Wise King, succeeded; envoys brought an investiture edict, seals and ribbons, caps, three red robes, child-sized swords and belts, and four thousand bolts of silk for distribution among kings and marquises.

sentences.zh: 其后单于薨，吊祭慰赐，以此为常。

translations.literal: Afterward when Chanyu died, mourning sacrifice consolation grants—by this became regular.
translations.idiomatic: Later deaths of chanyus drew the same mourning missions and stipends as precedent.

sentences.zh: 丘浮尤鞮单于莫，中元元年立，一年薨，弟汗立。

translations.literal: Qiufuyoudi Chanyu Mo, Zhongyuan first year enthroned; one year died; younger brother Han succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Qiufuyoudi Chanyu Mo took the throne in Zhongyuan 1 (56 CE), died the next year, and his brother Han succeeded.

sentences.zh: 伊伐于虑鞮单于汗，中元二年立。

translations.literal: Yifayulüdi Chanyu Han, Zhongyuan second year enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Yifayulüdi Chanyu Han was enthroned in Zhongyuan 2 (57 CE).

sentences.zh: 永平二年，北匈奴护于丘率众千余人来降。

translations.literal: Yongping second year, Northern Xiongnu Huyuqiu led crowd over one thousand persons came submit.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongping 2 (59 CE) the northern officer Huyuqiu brought more than a thousand men to surrender.

sentences.zh: 南部单于汗立二年薨，单于比之子適立。

translations.literal: Southern Chanyu Han, having ruled two years, died; Chanyu Bi’s son Shi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Han of the south ruled two years and died; Bi’s son Shi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 䤈僮尸逐侯鞮单于適，永平二年立。

translations.literal: Hitongshizhuhoudi Chanyu Shi, Yongping second year enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Hitongshizhuhoudi Chanyu Shi was enthroned in Yongping 2.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，北匈奴六七千骑入于五原塞，遂寇云中，至原阳。

translations.literal: Fifth year winter, Northern Xiongnu six or seven thousand riders entered into Wuyuan pass—thereupon raided Yunzhong, arrived Yuanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of year 5 some six or seven thousand northern riders breached Wuyuan and raided Yunzhong as far as Yuanyang.

sentences.zh: 南单于击却之，西河长史马襄赴救，虏乃引去。

translations.literal: Southern Chanyu struck and repelled them; Xihe Chief Clerk Ma Xiang hastened relief—the enemy then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Chanyu drove them back; Xihe chief clerk Ma Xiang reinforced him and the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 单于適立四年薨，单于莫子苏立，是为丘除车林鞮单于。

translations.literal: Chanyu Shi, having ruled four years, died; Chanyu Mo’s son Su succeeded—this is Qiuchuchelindi Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi ruled four years and died; Mo’s son Su became Qiuchuchelindi Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 敏月复薨，单于適之弟长立。

translations.literal: Within months again died; Chanyu Shi’s younger brother Zhang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died within months; Shi’s brother Zhang succeeded.

sentences.zh: 胡邪尸逐侯鞮单于长，永平六年立。

translations.literal: Hexieshizhuhoudi Chanyu Zhang, Yongping sixth year enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Hexieshizhuhoudi Chanyu Zhang was enthroned in Yongping 6 (63 CE).

sentences.zh: 时北匈奴犹盛，数寇边，朝廷以为忧。

translations.literal: At that time Northern Xiongnu still strong, repeatedly raided frontier—court took it as worry.
translations.idiomatic: The north was still strong and raided often; the court fretted over the frontier.

sentences.zh: 会北单于欲合市，遣使求和亲，显宗冀其交通，不复为寇，乃许之。

translations.literal: When Northern Chanyu wished joint market, dispatched envoys begging marriage alliance—Emperor Xianzong hoped they would communicate—no longer be raiders—thereupon permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Chanyu asked to trade and offered marriage ties; Emperor Ming hoped exchange would stop raids and agreed.

sentences.zh: 八年，遣越骑司马郑众北使报命，而南部须卜骨都侯等知汉与北虏交使，怀嫌怨欲畔，密因北使，令遣兵迎之。

translations.literal: Eighth year, dispatched Swift Cavalry Major Zheng Zhong north envoy return mission—but Southern Xubu Gudu Marquis and others knew Han and Northern enemy exchanged envoys, harbored grievance wished rebel—secretly through northern envoy, ordered dispatch troops welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 Zheng Zhong rode north on reciprocation; southern nobles like the Xubu Gudu Marquis, learning of Han–north diplomacy, plotted revolt and secretly asked northern envoys to send troops to fetch them.

sentences.zh: 郑众出塞，疑有异，伺候果得须卜使人，乃上言宜更置大将，以防二虏交通。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhong exited pass—suspected anomaly—waited watch—indeed obtained Xubu’s envoy—thereupon memorialized saying fitting to anew establish great general—to guard against two enemies communicating.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the wall Zheng sensed trouble, waited, caught Xubu’s messenger, and urged a new supreme commander to block collusion between north and south.

sentences.zh: 由是始置度辽营，以中郎将吴棠行度辽将军事，副校尉来苗、左校尉阎章、右校尉张国将黎阳虎牙营士，屯五原曼柏。

translations.literal: From this began establish Liaodu camp—using Commandant of Gentlemen of Household Wu Tang to act Liaodu general military affairs; Vice Colonel Lai Miao, Left Colonel Yan Zhang, Right Colonel Zhang Guo led Liyang Tiger-Fang camp soldiers—station Wuyuan Manbai.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Liaodu garrison: Colonel Wu Tang acting as Liaodu general with colonels Lai Miao, Yan Zhang, and Zhang Guo leading Liyang’s Tiger Guard at Manbai in Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 又遣骑都尉秦彭将兵屯美稷。

translations.literal: Also dispatched Cavalry Commandant Qin Peng lead troops station Meiji.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry commandant Qin Peng camped at Meiji.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，北虏果遣二千骑候望朔方，作马革船，欲度迎南部畔者，以汉有备，乃引去。

translations.literal: That year autumn, Northern enemy indeed dispatched two thousand riders scout-watch Shuofang—made horse-hide boats—wished cross welcome Southern rebels—because Han had preparations—thereupon led away.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn two thousand northern riders scouted Shuofang and built hide boats to ferry southern defectors; finding Han ready, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 复数寇抄边郡，焚烧城邑，杀略甚众，河西城门昼闭，帝患之。

translations.literal: Again repeatedly raided plundered border commanderies—burned cities—killed plundered very many—Hexi city gates day closed—emperor worried it.
translations.idiomatic: They kept pillaging: towns burned, many dead or taken; Hexi barred its gates by day, and the emperor fretted.

sentences.zh: 十六年，乃大发缘边兵，遣诸将四道出塞，北征匈奴。

translations.literal: Sixteenth year—thereupon greatly mobilized along-border troops—dispatched various generals four routes exit passes—north campaign Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 the court mobilized the frontier and sent four columns beyond the wall against the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 南单于遣左贤王信随太仆祭肜及吴棠出朔方高阙，攻皋林温禺犊王于涿邪山。

translations.literal: Southern Chanyu dispatched Left Wise King Xin following Grand Coachman Ji Tong and Wu Tang exit Shuofang Gaoque—attack Gaolin Wenyu-du king at Zhuoxie mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Chanyu sent Left Wise King Xin with Ji Tong and Wu Tang through Gaoque to strike the Gaolin Wenyu-du king on Mount Zhuoxie.

sentences.zh: 虏闻汉兵来，悉度漠去。

translations.literal: Enemy heard Han troops came—all crossed desert gone.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Han troops, they fled across the desert.

sentences.zh: 肜、棠坐不至涿邪山免，以骑都尉来苗行度辽将军。

translations.literal: Tong, Tang sit crime not reached Zhuoxie mountain dismissed—using Cavalry Commandant Lai Miao act Liaodu general.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Tong and Wu Tang were cashiered for never reaching Zhuoxie; cavalry commandant Lai Miao became acting Liaodu general.

sentences.zh: 其年，北匈奴入云中，遂至渔阳，太守廉范击却之。

translations.literal: That year, Northern Xiongnu entered Yunzhong—thereupon arrived Yuyang—prefect Lian Fan struck repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: The same year northerners pushed into Yunzhong and Yuyang until Prefect Lian Fan drove them back.

sentences.zh: 诏遣使者高弘发三郡兵追之，无所得。

translations.literal: Edict dispatched envoy Gao Hong mobilize three commanderies troops pursue them—obtained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy Gao Hong led three commanderies in pursuit but caught nothing.

sentences.zh: 建初元年，来苗迁济阴太守，以征西将军耿秉行度辽将军。

translations.literal: Jianchu first year, Lai Miao transferred Jiyin prefect—using Campaign-West General Geng Bing act Liaodu general.
translations.idiomatic: Jianchu 1 (76 CE): Lai Miao became prefect of Jiyin; campaign-general Geng Bing acted as Liaodu general.

sentences.zh: 时皋林温禺犊王复将众还居涿邪山，南单于闻知，遣轻骑与缘边郡及乌桓兵出塞击之，斩首数百级，降者三四千人。

translations.literal: At that time Gaolin Wenyu-du king again led crowd return dwell Zhuoxie mountain—Southern Chanyu heard knew—dispatched light cavalry with along-border commanderies and Wuhuan troops exit pass strike them—beheaded heads several hundred grades—submitters three or four thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaolin Wenyu-du king moved back to Zhuoxie, the Southern Chanyu sent light horse with frontier troops and Wuhuan allies; they took hundreds of heads and three or four thousand surrendered.

sentences.zh: 其年，南部苦蝗，大饥，肃宗禀给其贫人三万余口。

translations.literal: That year, Southern suffered locusts—great famine—Emperor Suzong granary-granted their poor persons three ten-thousand-plus mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts and famine struck the south; Emperor Zhang issued grain to more than thirty thousand needy people.

sentences.zh: 七年，耿秉迁执金吾，以张掖太守邓鸿行度辽将军。

translations.literal: Seventh year, Geng Bing transferred Bearer of the Mace—using Zhangye prefect Deng Hong act Liaodu general.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 Geng Bing became Bearer of the Mace; Zhangye prefect Deng Hong acted as Liaodu general.

sentences.zh: 八年，北匈奴三木楼訾大人稽留斯等，率三万八千人、马二万匹、牛、羊十余万，款五原塞降。

translations.literal: Eighth year, Northern Xiongnu Sanmulouzi great men Jiliusi and others—led thirty-eight thousand persons, horses twenty thousand head, cattle sheep over one hundred thousand—knocked Wuyuan pass submit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 northern chiefs such as Jiliusi of Sanmulouzi brought thirty-eight thousand people, twenty thousand horses, and huge herds to surrender at Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，武威太守孟云上言北单于复愿与吏人合市，诏书听云遣驿使迎呼慰纳之。

translations.literal: Yuanhe first year, Wuwei prefect Meng Yun memorialized Northern Chanyu again wished with clerk people joint market—imperial edict heard Yun dispatch relay riders welcome call console admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe 1 (84 CE): Wuwei’s Meng Yun reported the Northern Chanyu wanted frontier markets again; the edict let him send riders to welcome and host them.

sentences.zh: 北单于乃遣大且渠伊莫訾王等，驱牛、马万余头来与汉贾客交易。

translations.literal: Northern Chanyu then dispatched Great Juqu Yimozi Wang and others—drove cattle horses over ten thousand head come trade with Han merchant guests.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Chanyu sent nobles such as the Yimozi king with over ten thousand cattle and horses to trade with Han merchants.

sentences.zh: 诸王大人或前至，所在郡县为设官邸，赏赐待遇之。

translations.literal: Various kings great men some arrived first—where located commanderies counties for them set official lodges—reward grants treat receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever chiefs arrived, counties opened hostels and showered them with gifts.

sentences.zh: 南单于闻，乃遣轻骑出上郡，遮略生口，抄掠牛、马，驱还入塞。

translations.literal: Southern Chanyu heard—thereupon dispatched light cavalry exit Shang commandery—intercept plunder living mouths—raid plunder cattle horses—drive return enter pass.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Chanyu answered by raiding Shang commandery for captives and livestock and hurrying back inside the wall.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，北匈奴大人车利、涿兵等亡来入塞，凡七十三辈。

translations.literal: Second year first month, Northern Xiongnu great men Cheli, Zhuobing and others fled came enter pass—in all seventy-three batches.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yuanhe 2 chiefs such as Cheli and Zhuobing crossed the wall in seventy-three groups.

sentences.zh: 时北虏衰耗，党众离畔，南部攻其前，丁零寇其后，鲜卑击其左，西域侵其右，不复自立，乃远引而去。

translations.literal: At that time Northern enemy declining wasting—faction crowds separate rebel—Southern attacked their front—Dingling raided their rear—Xianbei struck their left—Western Regions invaded their right—no longer able establish self—thereupon far drew away gone.
translations.idiomatic: The north was failing: tribes split; the south pressed from ahead, Dingling from behind, Xianbei on the left, the Western Regions on the right—unable to hold ground, they withdrew far away.

sentences.zh: 单于长立二十三年薨，单于汗之子宣立。

translations.literal: Chanyu Zhang, having ruled twenty-three years, died—Chanyu Han’s son Xuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang ruled twenty-three years and died; Han’s son Xuan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 伊屠於闾鞮单于宣，元和二年立。

translations.literal: Yituyulüdi Chanyu Xuan, Yuanhe second year enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Yituyulüdi Chanyu Xuan took the throne in Yuanhe 2.

sentences.zh: 其岁，单于遣兵千余人猎至涿邪山，卒与北虏温禺犊王遇，因战，获其首级而还。

translations.literal: That year, Chanyu dispatched troops over one thousand persons hunt arrived Zhuoxie mountain—suddenly with Northern enemy Wenyu-du king met—thereupon battle—obtained his head-level and returned.
translations.idiomatic: That year he sent a thousand hunters to Zhuoxie and ran into the northern Wenyu-du king; they fought and brought back his head.

sentences.zh: 冬，孟云上言：“北虏以前既和亲，而南部复往抄掠，北单于谓汉欺之，谋欲犯塞，谓宜还南所掠生口，以慰安其意。

translations.literal: Winter, Meng Yun memorialized: “Northern enemy previously already marriage alliance—but Southern again went raid plunder—Northern Chanyu says Han deceives him—plots wish violate passes—deem fitting return South’s plundered living mouths—to console pacify his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Winter: Meng Yun warned that after peace was sealed the south kept raiding, so the Northern Chanyu thought Han had betrayed him and planned to strike the passes—best return the captives the south had taken to soothe him.

sentences.zh: ”肃宗从太仆袁安议，许之。

translations.literal: ” Emperor Suzong followed Grand Coachman Yuan An’s deliberation—permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: ” Emperor Zhang accepted Grand Coachman Yuan An and agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃下诏曰：“昔猃狁、獯粥之敌中国，其所由来尚矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon issued edict saying: “Formerly Xianyun, Xunyu’s opposing China—its origin goes back far.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then proclaimed: “Since antiquity Xianyun and the northern tribes have contested the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 往者虽有和亲之名，终无丝发之效。

translations.literal: In the past although there was marriage alliance’s name—ultimately no silk-thread hair’s effect.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage alliances brought only the name of peace, never the slightest real calm.

sentences.zh: 墝埆之人，屡婴涂炭。

translations.literal: Barren-stony land’s people—repeatedly suffer mud-charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier folk again and again drowned in slaughter.

sentences.zh: 父战于前，子死于后。

translations.literal: Father battles in front—son dies behind.
translations.idiomatic: Fathers fell in the van while sons died behind them.

sentences.zh: 弱女乘于亭障，孤兒号于道路。

translations.literal: Weak girls mounted on pavilion barriers—orphans cry on roads.
translations.idiomatic: Girls were dragged onto the ramparts and orphans wailed along the roads.

sentences.zh: 老母寡妻设虚祭，饮泣泪，想望归魂于沙漠之表，岂不哀哉！

translations.literal: Old mothers widowed wives set empty sacrifices—drink weep tears—longingly gaze return souls beyond desert’s edge—is it not pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: Mothers and widows offered empty rites, weeping for bones lost beyond the sands—could grief run deeper?

sentences.zh: 传曰：‘江海所以能长百川者，以其下之也。

translations.literal: Tradition says: ‘Rivers seas reason able grow hundred streams—is because they lower themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The classics say the rivers and seas stay great because they lie below every stream.’

sentences.zh: ’少加屈下，尚何足病？

translations.literal: ’ Slightly add bending low—still what worth sickness?
translations.idiomatic: A little humility costs nothing shameful.

sentences.zh: 况今与匈奴君臣分定，辞顺约明，贡献累至，岂宜违信，自受其曲？

translations.literal: Moreover now with Xiongnu lord-minister portions settled—words compliant covenant clear—tribute offerings accumulate arrive—how fitting violate trust—self receive its crookedness?
translations.idiomatic: Today lord and vassal stand defined, words are courteous and oaths plain, tribute keeps arriving—how could we break faith and wear the wrong?

sentences.zh: 其敕度辽及领中郎将庞奋倍雇南部所得生口，以还北虏。

translations.literal: Order Liaodu and Colonel of Gentlemen of Household Pang Fen double-hire Southern obtained living mouths—to return Northern enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Order Liaodu and Colonel Pang Fen to ransom at double rate every captive the south holds and hand them back to the north.

sentences.zh: 其南部斩首获生，计功受赏如常科。

translations.literal: As for Southern beheading heads capturing living—reckon merit receive reward like usual statute.
translations.idiomatic: Southern kills and captures will earn rewards under the usual rules.

sentences.zh: ”于是南单于复令薁鞮日逐王师子将轻骑数千出塞掩击北虏，复斩获千人。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Southern Chanyu again ordered Audiri Rizhu Wang Shizi lead light cavalry several thousand exit pass surprise strike Northern enemy—again beheaded captured thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Southern Chanyu then sent the Rizhu king Shizi with thousands of horse to ambush the north and took another thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 北虏众以南部为汉所厚，又闻取降者岁数千人。

translations.literal: Northern enemy crowds because Southern is by Han thick—also hear take surrenderers year several thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Northerners believed Han favored the south and drew thousands of defectors yearly.

sentences.zh: 章和元年，鲜卑入左地击北匈奴，大破之，斩优留单于，取其匈奴皮而还。

translations.literal: Zhanghe first year, Xianbei entered left territory strike Northern Xiongnu—greatly broke them—beheaded Youliu Chanyu—took his Xiongnu skin and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhanghe 1 (87 CE) the Xianbei struck from the left, routed the north, killed Youliu Chanyu, and carried off the royal skin banner.

sentences.zh: 北庭大乱，屈兰、储卑、胡都须等五十八部，口二十万，胜兵八千人，诣云中、五原、朔方、北地降。

translations.literal: Northern Court great chaos—Qulan, Chubei, Huduxu and others fifty-eight divisions—mouths two hundred thousand—victorious troops eight thousand persons—went Yunzhong, Wuyuan, Shuofang, Beidi submit.
translations.idiomatic: The northern court collapsed; fifty-eight tribes led by Qulan, Chubei, and Huduxu—two hundred thousand people, eight thousand fighters—surrendered at Yunzhong, Wuyuan, Shuofang, and Beidi.

sentences.zh: 单于宣立三年薨，单于长之弟屯屠何立。

translations.literal: Chanyu Xuan, having ruled three years, died—Chanyu Zhang’s younger brother Tun Tuhe succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan ruled three years and died; Zhang’s brother Tun Tuhe succeeded.

sentences.zh: 休兰尸逐侯鞮单于屯屠何，章和二年立。

translations.literal: Xiulanshizhuhoudi Chanyu Tun Tuhe, Zhanghe second year enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiulanshizhuhoudi Chanyu Tun Tuhe was enthroned in Zhanghe 2 (88 CE).

sentences.zh: 畤北虏大乱，加以饥蝗，降者前后而至。

translations.literal: When Northern enemy great chaos—add famine locusts—submitters front and rear arrived.
translations.idiomatic: As the north collapsed amid famine and locusts, surrendering bands streamed in.

sentences.zh: 南单于将并北庭，会肃宗崩，窦太后临朝。

translations.literal: Southern Chanyu about to merge Northern Court—when Suzong died—Empress Dowager Dou faced court.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Chanyu was poised to absorb the northern court when Emperor Zhang died and Empress Dowager Dou ruled from behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 其年七月，单于上言：

translations.literal: That year seventh month, Chanyu memorialized saying:
translations.idiomatic: That July the Chanyu petitioned:

sentences.zh: 臣累世蒙恩，不可胜数。

translations.literal: Your servant successive generations receive grace—not able fully count.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant’s house has received grace beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 孝章皇帝圣思远虑，遂欲见成就，故令乌桓、鲜卑讨北虏，斩单于首级，破坏其国。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhang sagely thought far planning—thereupon wished see accomplishment—therefore ordered Wuhuan, Xianbei campaign Northern enemy—beheaded Chanyu head-level—destroyed break their state.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhang looked far ahead and meant to finish the work: he set Wuhuan and Xianbei on the north, struck off a chanyu’s head, and shattered their realm.

sentences.zh: 今所新降虚渠等诣臣自言：“去岁三月中发虏庭，北单于创刈南兵，又畏丁令、鲜卑、遁逃远去，依安侯河西。

translations.literal: Now those newly submitted Xuqu and others came to your servant self saying: “Last year third month middle set out from enemy court—Northern Chanyu wounded mowed Southern troops—also feared Dingling, Xianbei—fled escaped far gone—rely Anhou west of river.
translations.idiomatic: New surrenderers such as Xuqu tell me: ‘Last March we left the northern court; our Chanyu was cut down fighting the south, then fled Dingling and Xianbei pressure to the west of the river by Anhou.’

sentences.zh: 今年正月，骨都侯等复共立单于异母兄右贤王为单于，其人以兄弟争立，并各离散。

translations.literal: This year first month, Gudu marquises again together enthroned Chanyu’s half-brother Right Wise King as Chanyu—those men because brothers contended for rule—together each scattered apart.
translations.idiomatic: This New Year the Gudu marquises set up the Chanyu’s half-brother, the Right Wise King; rival brothers tore the realm apart and followers scattered.

sentences.zh: ”臣与诸王骨都侯及新降渠帅杂议方略，皆曰宜及北虏分争，出兵讨伐，破北成南，并为一国，令汉家长无北念。

translations.literal: ” Your servant with various kings Gudu marquises and newly submitted chieftains mixed deliberated strategy—all said fitting seize while Northern enemy divides contends—dispatch troops campaign punish—break north complete south—merge as one state—make Han house long without northern thought.
translations.idiomatic: ’ I met with kings, marquises, and new surrender chiefs: take them while they fight among themselves, strike the north and seal the south as one realm so Han need never fear the steppe again.

sentences.zh: 又今月八日，新降右须日逐鲜堂轻从虏庭远来诣臣，言北虏诸部多欲内顾，但耻自发遣，故未有至者。

translations.literal: Also this month eighth day, newly submitted Right Xu Rizhu Xiantangqing from enemy court far came to your servant—said Northern enemy various divisions mostly wish turn inward—but ashamed self dispatch—therefore not yet arrivers.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth, the new defector Xiantangqing of the Right Xu Rizhu came from the northern court and said many tribes wish to come over but shrink from asking—so none have arrived.

sentences.zh: 若出兵奔击，必有响应。

translations.literal: If dispatch troops dash strike—certainly will have echoing response.
translations.idiomatic: A swift strike would draw allies out of the woodwork.

sentences.zh: 今年不往，恐复并壹。

translations.literal: This year not go—fear again merge unite.
translations.idiomatic: Wait another year and they may reunite.

sentences.zh: 臣伏念先父归汉以来，被蒙覆载，严塞明侯，大兵拥护，积四十年。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly reflects since former father returned Han onward—received cover load—strict passes bright marquises—great troops protect uphold—accumulated forty years.
translations.idiomatic: Since my father submitted, Han has sheltered us—guarded passes, honored titles, garrisoned troops—for forty years.

sentences.zh: 臣等生长汉地，开口仰食，岁时赏赐，动辄亿万，虽垂拱安枕，惭无报效之地。

translations.literal: Your servant et al. born grow Han land—open mouth look-up eat—year-season reward grants—move then hundred million—although drape arms secure pillow—ashamed no repay-effort ground.
translations.idiomatic: We grew up on Han grain and yearly gifts beyond counting; we sleep easy yet burn with shame that we have nothing to give back.

sentences.zh: 愿发国中及诸部故胡、新降精兵，遣左谷蠡王师子、左呼衍日逐王须訾将万骑出朔方，左贤王安国、右大且渠王交勒苏将万骑出居延，期十二月同会虏地。

translations.literal: Wish dispatch within state and various divisions old Hu, newly submitted crack troops—dispatch Left Guyuli King Shizi, Left Huyan Rizhu King Xuzi lead ten thousand riders exit Shuofang—Left Wise King Anguo, Right Great Juqu King Jiaolesu lead ten thousand riders exit Juyan—schedule twelfth month together meet enemy land.
translations.idiomatic: Mobilize our veterans and new allies: Left Guyuli Shizi and Left Huyan Rizhu Xuzi with ten thousand horse from Shuofang; Left Wise King Anguo and Right Great Juqu Jiaolesu with ten thousand from Juyan—to join in the twelfth month on steppe ground.

sentences.zh: 臣将余兵万人屯五原、朔方塞，以为拒守。

translations.literal: Your servant will lead remaining troops ten thousand men station Wuyuan, Shuofang passes—to take as resist guard.
translations.idiomatic: I will hold ten thousand men on the Wuyuan and Shuofang lines.

sentences.zh: 臣素愚浅，又兵众单少，不足以防内外。

translations.literal: Your servant plain foolish shallow—also troops crowd solitary few—not sufficient to guard internal external.
translations.idiomatic: I am no strategist and my forces are thin for inner and outer fronts.

sentences.zh: 愿遣执金吾耿秉、度辽将军邓鸿及西河、云中、五原、朔方、上郡太守并力而北，令北地、安定太守各屯要害，冀因圣帝威神，一举平定。

translations.literal: Wish dispatch Bearer of Mace Geng Bing, Liaodu General Deng Hong and Xihe, Yunzhong, Wuyuan, Shuofang, Shang prefects join strength northward—order Beidi, Anding prefects each station critical points—hope rely sagely emperor awe spirit—one rise pacify settle.
translations.idiomatic: Send Geng Bing, Deng Hong, and the frontier prefects north together; post Beidi and Anding on the choke points—by the emperor’s majesty end this in one blow.

sentences.zh: 臣国成败，要在今年。

translations.literal: Your servant state defeat victory—crux lies this year.
translations.idiomatic: Our fate turns on this year alone.

sentences.zh: 已敕诸部严兵马，讫九月龙祠，悉集河上。

translations.literal: Already ordered various divisions strict horses troops—until ninth month dragon sacrifice—all assemble river bank.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes are under arms; after the ninth-month dragon rite they mass on the river.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下裁哀省察！

translations.literal: Only Your Majesty cut pity examine inspect!
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to judge with mercy.

sentences.zh: 太后以示耿秉。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager thereby showed Geng Bing.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager showed the memorial to Geng Bing.

sentences.zh: 秉上言：“昔武帝单极天下，欲臣虏匈奴，未遇天时，事逐无成，宣帝之世，会呼韩来降，故边人获安，中外为一；

translations.literal: Bing memorialized saying: “Formerly Emperor Wu exhausted-extreme under Heaven—wished subject-captive Xiongnu—did not meet Heaven’s timing—affairs followed without completion—Emperor Xuan’s generation—when Huhanye came submit—therefore border people obtained peace—inside outside became one;
translations.idiomatic: Geng Bing replied: ‘Wu Di strained the empire to break the Xiongnu but heaven withheld success; under Xuan, when Huhanye yielded, the frontier rested and inner and outer realm became one.’

sentences.zh: 生人休息，六十余年。

translations.literal: Living people rested—sixty-plus years.
translations.idiomatic: For sixty years the people knew peace.

sentences.zh: 及王莽篡位，变更其号，耗扰不止，单于乃畔。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang usurped throne—changed alter his titles—waste harass did not cease—Chanyu then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang seized the throne, renamed titles, and ceaseless turmoil drove the Chanyu to revolt.

sentences.zh: 光武受命，复怀纳之，缘边坏郡得以还复。

translations.literal: Guangwu received mandate—again cherished admitted them—along-border ruined commanderies obtained thereby restore.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu renewed ties and welcomed them back; shattered march commands could be rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 乌桓、鲜卑，咸胁归义。

translations.literal: Wuhuan, Xianbei—all threatened submitted righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuan and Xianbei alike bent and pledged loyalty.

sentences.zh: 威镇四夷，其效如此。

translations.literal: Awe quelled four barbarians—its effect thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the awe that held the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 今幸遭天授，北虏分争，以夷伐夷，国家之利，宜可听许。

translations.literal: Now fortunately encounter Heaven’s grant—Northern enemy divides contends—use barbarian attack barbarian—state’s benefit—fitting can listen permit.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven now splits the north—let barbarian fight barbarian; it serves the empire and deserves approval.

sentences.zh: ”秉因自陈受恩，分当出命效用。

translations.literal: ” Bing thereby self stated received grace—portion ought emit life render effort.
translations.idiomatic: ’ He added that he owed everything to the throne and would stake his life on the campaign.

sentences.zh: 太后从之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager agreed.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，以秉为征西将军，与车骑将军窦宪率骑八千，与度辽兵及南单于众三万骑，出朔方击北虏，大破之。

translations.literal: Yongyuan first year—used Bing as Campaign-West General—with Chariots-and-Cavalry General Dou Xian lead riders eight thousand—with Liaodu troops and Southern Chanyu crowd thirty thousand riders—exit Shuofang strike Northern enemy—greatly broke them.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan 1 (89 CE) Geng Bing became campaign-general west; with Dou Xian’s eight thousand horse, Liaodu troops, and thirty thousand southern riders from Shuofang, they shattered the north.

sentences.zh: 北单于奔走，首虏二十余万人。

translations.literal: Northern Chanyu fled—heads captives over two hundred thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Chanyu fled; Han counted over two hundred thousand killed or taken.

sentences.zh: 事已具《窦宪传》。

translations.literal: Affairs already fully contained in ‘Dou Xian biography’.
translations.idiomatic: The rest is told in Dou Xian’s biography.

sentences.zh: 二年春，邓鸿迁大鸿□户，以定襄太守皇甫棱行度辽将军。

translations.literal: Second year spring—Deng Hong transferred Grand Hong[lacuna] Household—using Dingxiang prefect Huangfu Ling act Liaodu general.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 2 Deng Hong moved to the Grand Herald’s office (text damaged); Dingxiang prefect Huangfu Ling acted as Liaodu general.

sentences.zh: 南单于复上求灭北庭，于是遣左谷蠡王师子等将左右部八千骑出鸡鹿塞，中郎将耿谭遣从事将护之。

translations.literal: Southern Chanyu again memorialized begging destroy Northern Court—thereupon dispatched Left Guyuli King Shizi et al. lead left-right divisions eight thousand riders exit Jilu pass—Commandant of Gentlemen Geng Tan dispatched attendant-generals lead guard them.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Chanyu again asked to wipe out the northern court; Left Guyuli Shizi led eight thousand of both wings through Jilu pass while Colonel Geng Tan sent aides to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 至涿邪山，乃留辎重，分为二部，各引轻兵两道袭之。

translations.literal: Arrived Zhuoxie mountain—thereupon left baggage train—divided into two divisions—each led light troops two routes surprise strike them.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhuoxie they shed baggage, split in two, and struck along separate light columns.

sentences.zh: 左部北过西海至河云北，右部从匈奴河水西绕天山，南度甘微河，二军俱会，夜围北单于。

translations.literal: Left division north passed West Sea arrived Heyun north—Right division followed Xiongnu River water west circled Tianshan—south crossed Ganwei River—two armies together met—night surrounded Northern Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: The left wing rode north past the western sea to Heyun; the right followed the Xiongnu River west around the Celestial Mountains, crossed the Ganwei southward—and both closed by night around the Northern Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 单于大惊，率精兵千余人合战。

translations.literal: Chanyu greatly alarmed—led crack troops over one thousand men join battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu rallied over a thousand picked men and fought.

sentences.zh: 单于被创，堕马复上，将轻骑数十遁走，仅而免脱。

translations.literal: Chanyu received wound—fell horse again mounted—led light riders several tens fled escaped—barely thereby escaped free.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded, he fell and remounted, fled with dozens of horse, and barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 得其玉玺，获阏氏及男女五人，斩首八千级，生虏数千口而还。

translations.literal: Obtained his jade seal—captured Yan-zhi and male female five persons—beheaded heads eight thousand grades—living captives several thousand mouths—and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They seized his seal, his queen, five captives, eight thousand heads, and thousands taken alive.

sentences.zh: 是时南部连克获纳降，党众最盛，领户三万四千，口二十三万七千三百，胜兵五万一百七十。

translations.literal: At this time Southern repeatedly conquered captured admitted surrender—faction crowd most flourishing—commanding households thirty-four thousand—mouths two hundred thirty-seven thousand three hundred—victorious troops fifty thousand one hundred seventy.
translations.idiomatic: The south now drew victory after victory: thirty-four thousand households, 237,300 people, and 50,170 warriors under arms.

sentences.zh: 故事：中郎将置从事二人，耿谭以新降者多，上增从事十二人。

translations.literal: Old precedent: Commandant of Gentlemen installs attendant-generals two persons—Geng Tan because newly submitted many—memorialized increase attendant-generals twelve persons.
translations.idiomatic: By rule a colonel had two aides; Geng Tan, with many new tribesmen, won twelve more.

sentences.zh: 三年，北单于复为右校尉耿夔所破，逃亡不知所在。

translations.literal: Third year—Northern Chanyu again by Right Colonel Geng Kui struck broken—fled escaped not know where located.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Right Colonel Geng Kui broke the Northern Chanyu again; he vanished.

sentences.zh: 其弟右谷蠡王於降鞬自立为单于，将右温禺鞬王、骨都侯已下众数千人，止蒲类海，遣使款塞。

translations.literal: His younger brother Right Guyuli King Yujiangjian self-established as Chanyu—led Right Wen-yujian King, Gudu marquises downward crowd several thousand persons—stopped Pu-lei Sea—dispatched envoys knock passes.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yujiangjian, Right Guyuli, declared himself Chanyu with the Right Wen-yujian king, marquises, and thousands beside Lake Barkol; envoys knocked at the passes.

sentences.zh: 大将军窦宪上书，立於除鞬为北单于，朝廷从之。

translations.literal: Grand General Dou Xian memorialized—establish Yuchujian as Northern Chanyu—court followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Dou Xian asked to recognize Yuchujian as Northern Chanyu; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 四年，遣耿夔即授玺绶，赐玉剑四具，羽盖一驷，使中郎将任尚持节卫护屯伊吾，如南单于故事。

translations.literal: Fourth year—dispatched Geng Kui immediately grant seal-cords—grant jade swords four sets—feather canopy one four-horse team—order Commandant Ren Shang hold insignia guard protect station Yiwu—like Southern Chanyu old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Geng Kui invested him with seals, four jade swords, and a feather-canopied carriage; Colonel Ren Shang escorted him to Yiwu by southern precedent.

sentences.zh: 方欲辅归北庭，会窦宪被诛。

translations.literal: Just about to assist return Northern Court—when Dou Xian executed.
translations.idiomatic: They meant to restore him to the northern court—then Dou Xian was executed.

sentences.zh: 五年，於除鞬自畔还北，帝遣将兵长史王辅以千余骑与任尚共追，诱将还斩之。

translations.literal: Fifth year—Yuchujian self rebelled returned north—emperor dispatched Troop-leading Chief Clerk Wang Fu with over one thousand riders together with Ren Shang jointly pursue—lure lead return beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 Yuchujian rebelled and fled north; Chief Clerk Wang Fu and Ren Shang overtook him with a thousand horse, lured him back, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 破灭其众。

translations.literal: Destroyed extinguished his crowd.
translations.idiomatic: His following was crushed.

sentences.zh: 单于屯屠何立六年薨，单于宣弟安国立。

translations.literal: Chanyu Tun Tuhe, having ruled six years, died—Chanyu Xuan’s younger brother Anguo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Tun Tuhe ruled six years and died; Xuan’s brother Anguo succeeded.

sentences.zh: 单于安国，永远五年立。

translations.literal: Chanyu Anguo—Yongyuan fifth year enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Chanyu Anguo was enthroned in Yongyuan 5 (93 CE).

sentences.zh: 安国初为左贤王而无称誉。

translations.literal: Anguo at first was Left Wise King but without praise reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo had been Left Wise King without renown.

sentences.zh: 左谷蠡王师子素勇黠多知，前单于宣及屯屠何皆爱其气决，故数遣将兵出塞，掩击北庭，还受赏赐，天子亦加殊异。

translations.literal: Left Guyuli King Shizi plain brave crafty much knowledge—former Chanyu Xuan and Tun Tuhe both loved his qi resolve—therefore repeatedly dispatched lead troops exit pass—surprise strike Northern Court—return receive reward grants—Son of Heaven also added special unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guyuli Shizi was bold and shrewd; Xuan and Tun Tuhe prized his dash and sent him raiding the northern court again and again—rewards piled up and the emperor singled him out.

sentences.zh: 是以国中尽敬师子，而不附安国。

translations.literal: Therefore within state all revered Shizi—but did not attach Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: The realm sided with Shizi, not Anguo.

sentences.zh: 安国由是疾师子，欲杀之。

translations.literal: Anguo from this hated Shizi—wished kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo grew to hate Shizi and meant to kill him.

sentences.zh: 其诸新降胡初在塞外，数为师子所驱掠，皆多怨之。

translations.literal: Those various newly submitted Hu at first beyond passes—repeatedly by Shizi driven plundered—all much resented him.
