translations.idiomatic: New Hu beyond the wall had often suffered Shizi’s raids and bitterly resented him.

sentences.zh: 安国因是委计降者，与同谋议。

translations.literal: Anguo from this entrusted plans to surrenderers—with together plotted deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo took them into his counsels.

sentences.zh: 安国既立为单于，师子以次转为左贤王，觉单于与新降者有谋，乃别居五原界。

translations.literal: Anguo already established as Chanyu—Shizi by order turned Left Wise King—perceived Chanyu with newly submitted had plot—thereupon separately dwelt Wuyuan border.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, Anguo made Shizi Left Wise King; Shizi sensed a plot with the new tribesmen and moved apart within Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 单于每龙会议事，师子辄称病不往。

translations.literal: Chanyu each dragon assembly deliberated affairs—Shizi then claimed illness not go.
translations.idiomatic: At each dragon-rite council Shizi pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 皇甫棱知之，亦拥护不遣，单于怀愤益甚。

translations.literal: Huangfu Ling knew it—also protected upheld not dispatch—Chanyu harbored resentment ever more extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Ling backed him and would not send him; the Chanyu’s rage grew.

sentences.zh: 六年春，皇甫棱免，以执金吾硃徽行度辽将军。

translations.literal: Sixth year spring—Huangfu Ling dismissed—using Bearer of Mace Zhu Hui act Liaodu general.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 6 Huangfu Ling was removed; Bearer Zhu Hui acted as Liaodu general.

sentences.zh: 时单于与中郎将杜崇不相平，乃上书告崇，崇讽西河太守令断单于章，无由自闻。

translations.literal: At time Chanyu with Commandant Du Chong not mutually peaceful—thereupon memorialized reporting Chong—Chong hinted Xihe prefect order cut off Chanyu memorials—no route self heard.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu feuded with Colonel Du Chong and memorialized against him; Chong had the Xihe prefect stop the Chanyu’s petitions reaching court.

sentences.zh: 而崇因与硃徽上言：“南单于安国疏远故胡，亲近新降，欲杀左贤王师子及左台且渠刘利等。

translations.literal: And Chong thereby with Zhu Hui memorialized saying: “Southern Chanyu Anguo distant estranged old Hu—close intimate newly submitted—wishes kill Left Wise King Shizi and Left Terrace Juqu Liu Li et al.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and Zhu reported: ‘Anguo shuns the old Hu and favors new arrivals; he means to kill Left Wise King Shizi and Left Terrace Juqu Liu Li.’

sentences.zh: 又右部降者谋共迫胁安国，起兵背畔，诸西河、上郡、安定为之儆备。

translations.literal: Also Right division surrenderers plot together coerce Anguo—raise troops rebel betray—various Xihe, Shang, Anding for them alert prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Right-wing defectors plot to coerce Anguo into revolt; Xihe, Shang, and Anding stand ready.

sentences.zh: ”和帝下公卿议，皆以为“蛮夷反覆，虽难测知，然大兵聚会，必未敢动摇。

translations.literal: ” Emperor He sent down ministers deliberate—all deemed “Man-Yi reverse-repeat—although hard measure know—but great troops assemble meet—certainly not yet dare shake move.
translations.idiomatic: ’ Emperor He asked his ministers: barbarians are fickle, yet massed Han troops should hold them in check.

sentences.zh: 今宜遣有方略使者之单于庭，与杜崇、硃徽及西河太守并力，观其动静。

translations.literal: Now fitting dispatch have strategy-plan envoy go Chanyu court—with Du Chong, Zhu Hui and Xihe prefect join strength—observe their movement stillness.
translations.idiomatic: Send a capable envoy to the court with Chong, Zhu, and the Xihe prefect and watch what they do.

sentences.zh: 如无它变，可令崇等就安国会其左右大臣，责其部众横暴为边害者，共平罪诛。

translations.literal: If no other change—can order Chong et al. approach Anguo meet his left-right great ministers—demand his division crowds violent transgressive become border harmers—together settle guilt execute.
translations.idiomatic: If nothing stirs, have Chong join Anguo’s nobles, charge raiders who harm the frontier, and execute the guilty together.

sentences.zh: 若不从命，令为权时方略，事毕之后，裁行客赐，亦足以威示百蛮”。

translations.literal: If not obey orders—order make expedient-time strategy-plan—affairs finish afterward—trim conduct guest grants—also sufficient awe display hundred barbarians”.
translations.idiomatic: If they refuse, use interim measures; once done, trim rewards—enough to overawe the tribes.”

sentences.zh: 帝从之。

translations.literal: Emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 于是徽、崇遂发兵造其庭。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hui, Chong then dispatched troops arrive their court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu and Chong marched on the court.

sentences.zh: 安国夜闻汉军至，大惊，弃帐而去，因举兵及将新降者欲诛师子。

translations.literal: Anguo night heard Han army arrived—greatly alarmed—abandoned tent and departed—thereupon raised troops together with led newly submitted wished execute Shizi.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo fled his tent at news of Han troops, then rallied the new tribesmen to kill Shizi.

sentences.zh: 师子先知，乃悉将庐落入曼柏城。

translations.literal: Shizi beforehand knew—thereupon entirely led yurt gates enter Manbai city.
translations.idiomatic: Forewarned, Shizi withdrew every tent-line into Manbai.

sentences.zh: 安国追到城下，门闭不得入。

translations.literal: Anguo pursued arrived city below—gates closed not obtain enter.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo reached the walls but found the gates shut.

sentences.zh: 硃徽遣吏晓譬和之，安国不听。

translations.literal: Zhu Hui dispatched clerks dawn enlighten harmonize him—Anguo did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hui sent officers to reason with Anguo; he refused.

sentences.zh: 城既不下，乃引兵屯五原。

translations.literal: City already not taken—thereupon led troops station Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Failing to storm the city, he camped at Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 崇、徽因发诸郡骑追赴之急，众皆大恐，安国舅骨都侯喜为等虑并被诛，乃格杀安国。

translations.literal: Chong, Hui therefore dispatched various commanderies riders pursue hasten urgent—all greatly feared—Anguo uncle Gudu Marquis Xiwei et al. feared together would be executed—thereupon resisted killed Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and Zhu rushed cavalry from every command; panic spread until Anguo’s uncle Gudu Xiwei and others, fearing wholesale execution, slew Anguo.

sentences.zh: 安国立一年，单于適之子师子立。

translations.literal: Anguo established one year—Chanyu Shi’s son Shizi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo lasted one year; Shi’s son Shizi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 亭独尸逐侯鞮单于师子，永元六年立。

translations.literal: Tingdushizhuhoudi Chanyu Shizi—Yongyuan sixth year enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Tingdushizhuhoudi Chanyu Shizi was enthroned in Yongyuan 6 (94 CE).

sentences.zh: 降胡五六百人夜袭师子，安集掾王恬将卫护士与战，破之。

translations.literal: Submitted Hu five six hundred persons night surprise attacked Shizi—Anji aide Wang Tian led guard nurses battled—broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Five or six hundred surrendered Hu raided Shizi by night; registrar Wang Tian led his guards and routed them.

sentences.zh: 于是新降胡遂相惊动，十五部二十余万人皆反畔，胁立前单于屯屠何子薁鞬日逐王逢侯为单于，遂杀略吏人，燔烧邮亭庐帐，将车重向朔方，欲度漠北。

translations.literal: Thereupon newly submitted Hu then mutually alarmed move—fifteen divisions over two hundred thousand persons all rebel betray—coerced establish former Chanyu Tun Tuhe’s son Yujian Rizhu Wang Fenghou as Chanyu—thereupon killed plundered clerks people—burned postal pavilions yurt tents—led cart heavy toward Shuofang—wished cross desert north.
translations.idiomatic: The new tribes rose in panic: fifteen divisions, over two hundred thousand men, forced Fenghou, the Yujian Rizhu king and Tun Tuhe’s son, onto the throne; they slew officials, burned posts and camps, drove baggage toward Shuofang, and aimed for the northern desert.

sentences.zh: 于是遣行车骑将军邓鸿、越骑校尉冯柱、行度辽将军硃徽将左右羽林、北军五校士及郡国积射、缘边兵，乌桓校尉任尚将乌桓、鲜卑，合四万人讨之。

translations.literal: Thereupon dispatched acting Chariots-and-Cavalry General Deng Hong, Swift Cavalry Colonel Feng Zhu, acting Liaodu General Zhu Hui lead left-right Feathered Forest, Northern Army Five Corps soldiers and commandery-state stacked-shooters, along-border troops—Wuhuan Colonel Ren Shang lead Wuhuan, Xianbei—combined forty thousand persons campaign them.
translations.idiomatic: Acting general Deng Hong, colonels Feng Zhu and Zhu Hui led Guards, northern army corps, crossbowmen, and frontier troops; Wuhuan colonel Ren Shang brought Wuhuan and Xianbei—forty thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 时南单于及中郎将杜崇屯牧师城，逢侯将万余骑攻围之，未下。

translations.literal: At time Southern Chanyu and Commandant Du Chong stationed herdsman city—Fenghou led over ten thousand riders attack besieged it—not yet taken.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Chanyu and Du Chong held Herdsman City while Fenghou’s ten thousand horse besieged it without success.

sentences.zh: 冬，邓鸿等至美稷，逢侯乃乘冰度隘，向满夷谷。

translations.literal: Winter—Deng Hong et al. arrived Meiji—Fenghou then rode ice cross defile—toward Manyi valley.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Deng Hong reached Meiji; Fenghou crossed the ice through the pass toward Manyi valley.

sentences.zh: 南单于遣子将万骑，及杜崇所领四千骑，与邓鸿等追击逢侯于大城塞，斩首三千余级，得生口及降者万余人。

translations.literal: Southern Chanyu dispatched son lead ten thousand riders—and Du Chong led four thousand riders—with Deng Hong et al. pursue strike Fenghou at Great Wall pass—beheaded heads three thousand-plus grades—obtained living mouths and surrenderers over ten thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Chanyu’s son led ten thousand horse and Du Chong four thousand; with Deng Hong they ran Fenghou down at Dacheng pass—three thousand heads and over ten thousand captives or surrenders.

sentences.zh: 冯柱复分兵追击其别部，斩首四千余级。

translations.literal: Feng Zhu again divided troops pursue strike their separate division—beheaded heads four thousand-plus grades.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zhu split off to chase another wing and took four thousand more heads.

sentences.zh: 任尚率鲜卑大都护苏拔廆、乌桓大人勿柯八千骑，要击逢侯于满夷谷，复大破之。

translations.literal: Ren Shang led Xianbei Grand Protector Subagui, Wuhuan great man Wuke eight thousand riders—intercept strike Fenghou at Manyi valley—again greatly broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Shang with Subagui of the Xianbei and Wuke of the Wuhuan—eight thousand horse—ambushed Fenghou in Manyi valley and crushed him again.

sentences.zh: 前后凡斩万七千余级。

translations.literal: Front rear in all beheaded seventeen thousand-plus grades.
translations.idiomatic: The campaigns took more than seventeen thousand heads in all.

sentences.zh: 逢侯遂率众出塞，汉兵不能追。

translations.literal: Fenghou then led crowd exit pass—Han troops not able pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Fenghou escaped beyond the wall; Han could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，军还。

translations.literal: Seventh year first month—army returned.
translations.idiomatic: The army marched home in the first month of year 7.

sentences.zh: 冯柱将虎牙营留屯五原，罢遣鲜卑、乌桓、羌胡兵、封苏拔廆为率众王，又赐金、帛。

translations.literal: Feng Zhu led Tiger-Fang camp remain station Wuyuan—dismiss dispatch Xianbei, Wuhuan, Qiang Hu troops—enfeoff Subagui as Lead-Crowd King—also grant gold, silk.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zhu’s Tiger Guard stayed at Wuyuan; Xianbei, Wuhuan, and Qiang auxiliaries went home; Subagui was titled king of the host and given gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 邓鸿还京师，坐逗留失利，下狱死。

translations.literal: Deng Hong returned capital—sit crime loiter delay lose advantage—down prison died.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Hong reached the capital but was jailed and died for dallying and failure.

sentences.zh: 后帝知硃徽、杜崇失胡和，又禁其上书，以致反畔，皆征下狱死，以雁门太守庞奋行度辽将军。

translations.literal: Afterward emperor knew Zhu Hui, Du Chong lost Hu harmony—also forbade their memorials—thereby caused rebel betray—all summoned down prison died—using Yanmen prefect Pang Fen act Liaodu general.
translations.idiomatic: The court learned Zhu and Chong had ruined harmony with the Hu and blocked their petitions, provoking revolt; both were summoned and died in prison; Yanmen’s Pang Fen acted as Liaodu general.

sentences.zh: 逢侯于塞外分为二部，自领右部，屯涿邪山下。

translations.literal: Fenghou beyond pass divided into two divisions—self commanded Right division—stationed Zhuoxie mountain below.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the wall Fenghou split in two; he led the right wing below Mount Zhuoxie.

sentences.zh: 左部屯朔方西北，相去数百里。

translations.literal: Left division stationed Shuofang northwest—mutually apart several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The left wing camped northwest of Shuofang, hundreds of li away.

sentences.zh: 八年冬，左部胡自相疑畔，还入朔方塞，庞奋迎受，慰纳之。

translations.literal: Eighth year winter—Left division Hu mutually suspected rebel—returned enter Shuofang pass—Pang Fen welcomed received—consoled admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of year 8 the left wing turned on itself, re-entered Shuofang, and Pang Fen welcomed them in.

sentences.zh: 其胜兵四千人，弱小万余口，悉降，以分处北边诸郡。

translations.literal: Their victorious troops four thousand persons—weak small over ten thousand mouths—all surrendered—thereby divided dwell northern border various commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Four thousand fighters and over ten thousand dependents surrendered and were settled across the northern commanderies.

sentences.zh: 南单于以其右温禺犊王乌居战始与安国同谋，欲考问之。

translations.literal: Southern Chanyu because his Right Wenyu-du King Wuju Zhan at first with Anguo together plotted—wished examine interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Chanyu meant to question Wuju Zhan, Right Wenyu-du king, for conspiring with Anguo.

sentences.zh: 乌居战将数千人遂复反畔，出塞外山谷间，为吏民害。

translations.literal: Wuju Zhan led several thousand persons then again rebel betray—exited beyond pass mountain valleys between—became clerks people harm.
translations.idiomatic: Wuju Zhan rebelled with thousands and harried officials and folk from the hills beyond the wall.

sentences.zh: 秋，庞奋、冯柱与诸郡兵击乌居战，其众降，于是徙乌居战众及诸还降者二万余人于安定、北地。

translations.literal: Autumn—Pang Fen, Feng Zhu with various commanderies troops struck Wuju Zhan—their crowd surrendered—thereupon relocated Wuju Zhan crowd and various returned surrenderers over twenty thousand persons to Anding, Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Pang Fen and Feng Zhu crushed him; over twenty thousand followers were moved to Anding and Beidi.

sentences.zh: 冯柱还，迁将作大匠。

translations.literal: Feng Zhu returned—transferred Grand Artisan Builder.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zhu came back promoted to grand artisan.

sentences.zh: 逢侯部众饥穷，又为鲜卑所击，无所归，窜逃入塞者骆驿不绝。

translations.literal: Fenghou division crowds hungry poor—again by Xianbei struck—no place return—flee escape enter pass ones continuous unbroken.
translations.idiomatic: Starving and harried by the Xianbei, Fenghou’s people streamed through the passes without end.

sentences.zh: 单于师子立四年薨，单于长之子檀立。

translations.literal: Chanyu Shizi, having ruled four years, died—Chanyu Zhang’s son Tan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Shizi ruled four years and died; Zhang’s son Tan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 万氏尸逐鞮单于檀，永元十年立。

translations.literal: Wansishizhudi Chanyu Tan—Yongyuan tenth year enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Wansishizhudi Chanyu Tan was enthroned in Yongyuan 10 (98 CE).

sentences.zh: 十二年，庞奋迁河南尹，以朔方太守王彪行度辽将军。

translations.literal: Twelfth year—Pang Fen transferred Henan Intendant—using Shuofang prefect Wang Biao act Liaodu general.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 Pang Fen became intendant of Henan; Shuofang prefect Wang Biao acted as Liaodu general.

sentences.zh: 南单于比岁遣兵击逢侯，多所虏获，收还生口前后以千数，逢侯转困迫。

translations.literal: Southern Chanyu year-by-year dispatched troops strike Fenghou—much plunder capture—collect return living mouths front rear by thousand count—Fenghou turned distressed pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year the Southern Chanyu struck Fenghou, taking thousands of captives back until Fenghou was cornered.

sentences.zh: 十六年，北单于遣使诣阙贡献，愿和亲，修呼韩邪故约。

translations.literal: Sixteenth year—Northern Chanyu dispatched envoys arrive palace gate submit tribute—wish marriage alliance—restore Huhanye old covenant.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 the Northern Chanyu sent envoys with tribute, seeking marriage ties and renewal of Huhanye’s old pact.

sentences.zh: 和帝以其旧礼不备，未许之，而厚加赏赐，不答其使。

translations.literal: Emperor He because their old rites not complete—not permitted them—but thickly added reward grants—did not answer their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor He judged their protocol insufficient and withheld marriage ties; he sent rich gifts but no reply to their embassy.

sentences.zh: 元兴元年，重遣使诣敦煌贡献，辞以国贫未能备礼，愿请大使，当遣子入侍。

translations.literal: Yuanxing first year—again dispatched envoys arrive Dunhuang submit tribute—excused saying state poor not yet able complete rites—wished request great envoy—will dispatch son enter attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxing 1 (105 CE) they sent tribute to Dunhuang, pleading poverty and imperfect ceremony, asking for a senior envoy and offering to send a hostage son.

sentences.zh: 时邓太后临朝，亦不答其使，但加赐而已。

translations.literal: At time Empress Dowager Deng faced court—also did not answer their envoys—but added grants only.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Deng likewise ignored their envoys and increased gifts only.

sentences.zh: 永初三年夏，汉人韩琮随南单于入朝，既还，说南单于云：“关东水潦，人民饥饿死尽，可击也。

translations.literal: Yongchu third year summer—Han person Han Cong followed Southern Chanyu enter court—already returned—persuaded Southern Chanyu saying: “East of passes floodwaters—people/starving dead exhausted—can strike.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of Yongchu 3 (109 CE) Han Cong returned from court with the Southern Chanyu and told him: ‘East of the passes is drowned and starving—strike now.’

sentences.zh: ”单于信其言，遂起兵反畔，攻中郎将耿种于美稷。

translations.literal: ” Chanyu believed his words—thereupon raised troops rebel betray—attacked Commandant Geng Zhong at Meiji.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu believed him, rebelled, and struck Colonel Geng Zhong at Meiji.

sentences.zh: 秋，王彪卒。

translations.literal: Autumn—Wang Biao died.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Wang Biao died.

sentences.zh: 冬，遣行车骑将军何熙、副中郎将庞雄击之。

translations.literal: Winter—dispatched acting Chariots-and-Cavalry General He Xi, Vice Commandant Pang Xiong strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Winter brought acting general He Xi and Vice Colonel Pang Xiong against them.

sentences.zh: 四年春，檀遣千余骑寇常山、中山，以西域校尉梁慬行度辽将军， 与辽东太守耿夔击破之。

translations.literal: Fourth year spring—Tan dispatched over one thousand riders raid Changshan, Zhongshan—using Western Regions Colonel Liang Jin act Liaodu general—with Liaodong prefect Geng Kui struck broke them.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 4 Tan raided Changshan and Zhongshan with a thousand horse; Liang Jin as Liaodu general and Liaodong’s Geng Kui defeated him.

sentences.zh: 事已具《慬》、《夔传》。

translations.literal: Affairs already fully contained in ‘Liang Jin’, ‘Geng Kui’ biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Details appear in the biographies of Liang Jin and Geng Kui.

sentences.zh: 单于见诸军并进，大恐怖，顾让韩琮曰：“汝言汉人死尽，今是何等人也？

translations.literal: Chanyu saw various armies together advance—greatly terrified—turned rebuke Han Cong saying: “You said Han people dead exhausted—now are what sort persons?
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Han columns advance, the Chanyu panicked and rounded on Han Cong: ‘You said the Han were wiped out—who are these men?’

sentences.zh: ”乃遣使乞降，许之。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon dispatched envoys beg surrender—permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He sued for peace and Han accepted.

sentences.zh: 单于脱帽徒跣，对庞雄等拜，陈道死罪。

translations.literal: Chanyu removed cap barefoot—toward Pang Xiong et al. bowed—stated expressed capital guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Barefoot and bareheaded he bowed to Pang Xiong and confessed his capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 于是赦之，遇待如初，乃还所抄汉民男女及羌所略转卖入匈奴中者，合万余人。

translations.literal: Thereupon pardoned him—treated encounter as at first—thereupon returned those plundered Han commoner males females and Qiang those snatched resold entered Xiongnu within—combined over ten thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: He was pardoned and treated as before; over ten thousand Han taken in raids or sold through Qiang brokers were returned.

sentences.zh: 五年，梁慬免，以云中太守耿夔行度辽将军。

translations.literal: Fifth year—Liang Jin dismissed—using Yunzhong prefect Geng Kui act Liaodu general.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 Liang Jin was removed; Yunzhong prefect Geng Kui acted as Liaodu general.

sentences.zh: 无初元年，夔免，以乌桓校尉邓遵为度辽将军。

translations.literal: Wuchu first year—Kui dismissed—using Wuhuan Colonel Deng Zun as Liaodu general.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanchu 1 Geng Kui fell; Wuhuan colonel Deng Zun became Liaodu general.

sentences.zh: 遵，皇太后之从弟，故始为真将军焉。

translations.literal: Zun—Empress Dowager’s cousin younger brother—therefore first became true general therein.
translations.idiomatic: Zun was the empress dowager’s cousin—the first substantive appointment to the post.

sentences.zh: 四年，逢侯为鲜卑所破，部众分散，皆归北虏。

translations.literal: Fourth year—Fenghou by Xianbei struck broken—division crowds scattered—all returned Northern enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongjian 4 (129 CE) the Xianbei broke Fenghou; his bands scattered back to the northern court.

sentences.zh: 五年春，逢侯将百余骑亡还，诣朔方塞降，邓遵奏徙逢侯于颍川郡。

translations.literal: Fifth year spring—Fenghou led over hundred riders fled returned—went Shuofang pass submit—Deng Zun memorialized relocate Fenghou to Yingchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring Fenghou fled back with a hundred riders and surrendered at Shuofang; Deng Zun had him moved to Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 建光元年，邓遵免，复以耿夔代为度辽将军。

translations.literal: Jianguang first year—Deng Zun dismissed—again used Geng Kui replace as Liaodu general.
translations.idiomatic: Jianguang 1 (121 CE): Deng Zun out; Geng Kui again acted as Liaodu general.

sentences.zh: 时鲜卑冠边，夔与温禺犊王呼尤徽将新降者连年出塞，讨击鲜卑。

translations.literal: At time Xianbei raided border—Kui with Wenyu-du king Hu Youhui led newly submitted year after year exit pass—campaign strike Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: As the Xianbei raided, Geng Kui and Wenyu-du king Hu Youhui led new tribesmen out yearly against them.

sentences.zh: 还，复各令屯列冲要。

translations.literal: Returned—again each ordered station array critical points.
translations.idiomatic: On return they were posted again at key passes.

sentences.zh: 而耿夔征发烦剧，新降者皆悉恨谋畔。

translations.literal: But Geng Kui levy dispatch vexing intense—newly submitted all entirely resent plotted rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Kui’s relentless levies turned every new tribe toward revolt.

sentences.zh: 单于檀立二十七年薨，弟拔立。

translations.literal: Chanyu Tan, having ruled twenty-seven years, died—younger brother Ba succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Tan ruled twenty-seven years and died; his brother Ba succeeded.

sentences.zh: 耿夔复免，以太原太守法度代为将军。

translations.literal: Geng Kui again dismissed—using Taiyuan Grand Tutor Fa Du replace as general.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Kui fell again; Taiyuan grand tutor Fa Du became general.

sentences.zh: 乌稽侯尸逐鞮单于拔。

translations.literal: Wujihoushizhudi Chanyu Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Wujihoushizhudi Chanyu Ba.

sentences.zh: 延光三年立。

translations.literal: Yanguang third year enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: He was enthroned in Yanguang 3 (124 CE).

sentences.zh: 夏，新降一部大人阿族等遂反畔，胁呼尤徽欲与俱去。

translations.literal: Summer—newly submitted one division great man Azu et al. then rebel betray—coerced Hu Youhui wished together depart.
translations.idiomatic: That summer chief Azu’s band rebelled and tried to drag Hu Youhui away.

sentences.zh: 呼尤徽曰：“我老矣，受汉家恩，宁死不能相随！

translations.literal: Hu Youhui said: “I old already—received Han house grace—rather die cannot follow together!
translations.idiomatic: Hu Youhui said: ‘I am old and owe Han every kindness—I would die before I went with you!’

sentences.zh: ”众欲杀之，有救者，得免。

translations.literal: ” Crowd wished kill him—had rescuer—obtained escape.
translations.idiomatic: They nearly killed him until someone intervened.

sentences.zh: 阿族等遂将妻子辎重亡去，中郎将马翼遣兵与胡骑追击，破之，斩首及自投河死者殆尽，获马、牛、羊万余头。

translations.literal: Azu et al. then led wives children baggage train fled—Commandant Ma Yi dispatched troops with Hu riders pursue strike—broke them—beheaded heads and self cast river dead nearly exhausted—obtained horses cattle sheep over ten thousand head.
translations.idiomatic: Azu fled with families and baggage; Colonel Ma Yi ran them down—few survived the swords or the river—and took over ten thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 冬，法度卒。

translations.literal: Winter—Fa Du died.
translations.idiomatic: Fa Du died that winter.

sentences.zh: 四年，汉阳太守傅众代为将军。

translations.literal: Fourth year—Hanyang prefect Fu Zhong replace as general.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Hanyang prefect Fu Zhong succeeded as general.

sentences.zh: 其冬，傅众复卒。

translations.literal: That winter—Fu Zhong again died.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhong died the same winter.

sentences.zh: 永建元年，以辽东太守庞参代为将军。

translations.literal: Yongjian first year—using Liaodong prefect Pang Can replace as general.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjian 1 (126 CE): Liaodong prefect Pang Can became general.

sentences.zh: 先是，朔方以西障塞多不修复，鲜卑因此数冠南部，杀渐将王。

translations.literal: Before this—Shuofang west barrier passes mostly not repaired—Xianbei from this repeatedly raided Southern division—killed Jianjiang king.
translations.idiomatic: Barrier works west of Shuofang had long decayed; the Xianbei struck the south again and again and killed the Jianjiang king.

sentences.zh: 单于忧恐，上言求复障塞，顺帝从之。

translations.literal: Chanyu worried feared—memorialized beg restore barrier passes—Emperor Shun followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu petitioned in alarm to rebuild the forts; Emperor Shun agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃遣黎阳营兵出屯中山北界，增置缘边诸郡兵，列屯塞下，教习战射。

translations.literal: Thereupon dispatched Liyang camp troops exit station Zhongshan north border—increase establish along-border various commanderies troops—array station below passes—teach drill combat shoot.
translations.idiomatic: Liyang garrison troops moved to Zhongshan’s north march; frontier commands were reinforced along the wall with drill in arms and archery.

sentences.zh: 单于拔立四年薨，弟休利立。

translations.literal: Chanyu Ba, having ruled four years, died—younger brother Xiuli succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Ba ruled four years and died; his brother Xiuli succeeded.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，南匈奴左部句龙王吾斯、车纽等背叛，率三千余骑寇西河，因复招诱右贤王，合七八千骑围美稷，杀朔方、代郡长史。

translations.literal: Fifth year summer—Southern Xiongnu Left Division Goulong king Wusi, Cheniu et al. betray—led three thousand-plus riders raid Xihe—thereupon again enticed Right Wise King—combined seven eight thousand riders besiege Meiji—killed Shuofang, Dai chief clerks.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Wusi and Cheniu of the left Goulong band rebelled with three thousand horse in Xihe, pulled in the Right Wise King, and seven or eight thousand riders besieged Meiji, killing the Shuofang and Dai chief clerks.

sentences.zh: 马续与中郎将梁并、乌桓校尉王元，发缘边兵及乌桓、鲜卑、羌胡，合二万余人，掩击破之。

translations.literal: Ma Xu with Commandant Liang Bing, Wuhuan Colonel Wang Yuan—mobilized along-border troops and Wuhuan, Xianbei, Qiang Hu—combined over twenty thousand persons—surprise strike broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xu with Liang Bing and Wang Yuan raised frontier troops, Wuhuan, Xianbei, and Qiang—over twenty thousand—and struck them by surprise.

sentences.zh: 吾斯等遂更屯聚，攻没城邑。

translations.literal: Wusi et al. then anew gathered massed—attacked sank cities.
translations.idiomatic: Wusi regrouped and took towns.

sentences.zh: 天子遣使责让单于，开以恩义，令相招降。

translations.literal: Son of Heaven dispatched envoys reproach Chanyu—open with grace righteousness—order mutually summon surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The throne rebuked the Chanyu yet urged grace and ordered him to summon surrender.

sentences.zh: 单于本不豫谋，乃脱帽避帐，诣并谢罪。

translations.literal: Chanyu originally not pre-plotted plot—thereupon removed cap avoided tent—went to Bing apologize guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu had not planned the revolt; he doffed his cap, left his yurt, and begged Liang Bing’s pardon.

sentences.zh: 并以病征，五原太守陈龟代为中郎将。

translations.literal: Bing because illness summoned—Wuyuan prefect Chen Gui replace as Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Bing was recalled ill; Wuyuan prefect Chen Gui became colonel.

sentences.zh: 龟以单于不能制下，逼迫之，单于及其弟左贤王皆自杀。

translations.literal: Gui because Chanyu not able control subordinates—pressed compelled him—Chanyu and his younger brother Left Wise King both self-killed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gui hounded the Chanyu for failing his people until he and the Left Wise King killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 单于林利立十三年。

translations.literal: Chanyu Linli ruled thirteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuli had ruled thirteen years.

sentences.zh: 龟又欲徙单于近亲于内郡，而降者遂更狐疑。

translations.literal: Gui again wished relocate Chanyu close kin to interior commanderies—and surrenderers then turned doubting hesitant.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gui also meant to move the Chanyu’s kin inland; the surrendered tribes grew wary.

sentences.zh: 龟坐下狱免。

translations.literal: Gui sit crime down prison dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gui was jailed and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 大将军梁商以羌胡新反，党众初合，难以兵服，宜用招降，乃上表曰：“匈奴寇畔，自知罪极。

translations.literal: Grand General Liang Shang because Qiang Hu newly rebelled—faction crowd first joined—hard use troops subdue—fitting use summon surrender—thereupon memorialized saying: “Xiongnu raid rebel—self know guilt extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Liang Shang argued fresh Qiang and Hu revolts needed persuasion not battle, and wrote: ‘The Xiongnu know their guilt is capital.’

sentences.zh: 穷鸟困兽，皆知救死，况种类繁炽，不可单尽。

translations.literal: Destitute bird trapped beast—all know save from death—moreover species types numerous flourishing—not able singly exhaust.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered birds and beasts fight for life; these tribes are many—you cannot exterminate them all.

sentences.zh: 今转运日增，三军疲苦，虚内给外，非中国之利。

translations.literal: Now transport transfer daily increase—Three Armies weary bitter—empty interior supply exterior—not Central States’ benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Convoys swell, the armies tire, and draining the interior for the frontier helps no one in China.

sentences.zh: 窃见度辽将军马续素有谋谟，且典边日久，深晓兵要，每得续书，与臣策合。

translations.literal: Privately see Liaodu General Ma Xu plain has strategy-planning—moreover manage border day long—deeply understand military essentials—each obtain Xu’s letters—with your servant’s strategy match.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodu general Ma Xu is a planner who knows the frontier; his letters always match my counsel.

sentences.zh: 宜令续深沟高壁，以恩信招降，宣示购赏，明其期约。

translations.literal: Fitting order Xu deep moats high walls—with grace trust summon surrender—display proclaim purchase rewards—clarify their period covenants.
translations.idiomatic: Have him dig in, win them by grace, post bounties, and set clear terms.

sentences.zh: 如此，则丑类可服，国家无事矣。

translations.literal: Like this—then ugly sorts can submit—state has no affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Then the rebels yield and the realm stays quiet.

sentences.zh: ”帝从之，乃诏续招降畔虏。

translations.literal: ” Emperor followed it—thereupon edict Xu summon surrender rebel captives.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered Ma Xu to accept surrenders.

sentences.zh: 商又移书续等曰：“中国安宁，忘战日久。

translations.literal: Shang again shifted letter Xu et al. saying: “Central States peaceful calm—forgot battle day long.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Ma Xu: ‘China has been at peace so long we forget war.’

sentences.zh: 良骑野合，交锋接矢，决胜当时，戎狄之所长，而中国之所短也。

translations.literal: Good riders wild join—cross blades catch arrows—decide victory that moment—Rong Di’s place excel—but Central States’ place short.
translations.idiomatic: Mounted skirmish in the open is where the nomads excel and we falter.

sentences.zh: 强弩乘城，坚营固守，以待其衰，中国之所长，而戎狄之所短也。

translations.literal: Strong crossbows mount walls—firm camps firmly guard—to await their decline—Central States’ place excel—but Rong Di’s place short.
translations.idiomatic: Strong crossbows, walls, and stubborn camps play to our strengths and their weaknesses.

sentences.zh: 宜务先所长，以观其变，设购开赏，宣示反悔，勿贪小功，以乱大谋。

translations.literal: Fitting pursue first place excel—to observe their changes—set purchase open rewards—display proclaim regret-turn—do not greed small merit—to disorder great plan.
translations.idiomatic: Lead with your strengths, watch how they shift, publish bounties and terms for repentance—do not chase petty kills and spoil the strategy.

sentences.zh: ”续及诸郡并各遵行。

translations.literal: ” Xu and various commanderies together each obeyed practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xu and the commanderies obeyed.

sentences.zh: 于是右贤王部抑鞮等万三千口诣续降。

translations.literal: Thereupon Right Wise King division Yidi et al. thirteen thousand mouths went Xu surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yidi of the Right Wise King’s wing brought thirteen thousand people to surrender to Ma Xu.

sentences.zh: 秋，句龙吾斯等立句龙王车纽为单于。

translations.literal: Autumn—Goulong Wusi et al. established Goulong king Cheniu as Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Wusi set up Cheniu as Goulong Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 东引乌桓，西收羌戎及诸胡等数万人，攻破京兆虎牙营，杀上郡都尉及军司马，遂寇掠并、凉、幽、冀四州。

translations.literal: East drew Wuhuan—west gathered Qiang Rong and various Hu et al. several tens thousand persons—broke Jingzhao Tiger-Fang camp—killed Shang commandant and army major—thereupon raided plundered Bing, Liang, You, Ji four provinces.
translations.idiomatic: They drew Wuhuan in the east and tens of thousands of Qiang and Hu in the west, stormed the Jingzhao Tiger Guard, killed Shang’s commandant and army major, and ravaged Bing, Liang, You, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 乃徙西河治离石，上郡治夏阳，朔方治五原。

translations.literal: Thereupon moved Xihe administration Lishi—Shang administration Xiayang—Shuofang administration Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xihe’s seat moved to Lishi, Shang’s to Xiayang, Shuofang’s to Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 冬，遣中郎将张耽将幽州乌桓诸郡营兵，击畔虏车纽等，战于马邑，斩首三千级，获生口及兵器、牛、羊甚众。

translations.literal: Winter—dispatched Commandant Zhang Dan lead Youzhou Wuhuan various commanderies camp troops—strike rebel captives Cheniu et al.—battled at Mayi—beheaded heads three thousand grades—obtained living mouths and weapons cattle sheep very many.
translations.idiomatic: Winter: Colonel Zhang Dan led Youzhou Wuhuan and camp troops against Cheniu at Mayi—three thousand heads plus captives, arms, and herds.

sentences.zh: 车纽等将诸豪帅骨都侯乞降，而吾斯犹率其部曲与乌桓寇抄。

translations.literal: Cheniu et al. led various heroic leaders Gudu marquises beg surrender—but Wusi still led his division bands with Wuhuan raid plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Cheniu’s chiefs offered surrender while Wusi still raided with Wuhuan.

sentences.zh: 六年春，马续率鲜卑五千骑到穀城击之，斩首数百级。

translations.literal: Sixth year spring—Ma Xu led Xianbei five thousand riders arrived Gucheng strike them—beheaded heads several hundred grades.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 6 Ma Xu took five thousand Xianbei horse to Gucheng and took hundreds of heads.

sentences.zh: 张耽性勇锐，而善抚士卒，军中皆为用命。

translations.literal: Zhang Dan nature brave sharp—and good soothe soldiers—within army all for used commands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dan was bold and won his men’s utter loyalty.

sentences.zh: 遂绳索相悬，上通天山，大破乌桓，悉斩其渠帅，还得汉民，获其畜生财物。

translations.literal: Thereupon ropes cords mutually suspended—up connected Tianshan—greatly broke Wuhuan—entirely beheaded their channel leaders—again obtained Han people—obtained their livestock goods wealth.
translations.idiomatic: They roped the cliffs to the Celestial Mountains, shattered the Wuhuan, slew every chief, freed Han captives, and seized herds and plunder.

sentences.zh: 夏，马续复免，以城门校尉吴武代为将军。

translations.literal: Summer—Ma Xu again dismissed—using City Gate Colonel Wu Wu replace as general.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Ma Xu fell again; City Gate colonel Wu Wu became general.

sentences.zh: 汉安元年秋，吾斯与薁鞮台耆、且渠伯德等复掠并部。

translations.literal: Han’an first year autumn—Wusi with Yujian Taiqi, Juqu Bode et al. again plundered Bing division.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of Han’an 1 (142 CE) Wusi with Taiqi and Bode raided Bing again.

sentences.zh: 呼兰若尸逐就单于兜楼储先在京师，汉安二年立之。

translations.literal: Hulanruoshizhujiu Chanyu Dou Louchu before at capital—Han’an second year enthroned him.
translations.idiomatic: Hulanruoshizhujiu Chanyu Dou Louchu had been at the capital; in Han’an 2 (143 CE) he was enthroned.

sentences.zh: 天子临轩，大鸿胪持节拜授玺绶，引上殿。

translations.literal: Son of Heaven faced porch—Grand Herald held insignia bow grant seal-cords—led ascend hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the porch; the Grand Herald invested him with seals and led him to the hall.

sentences.zh: 赐青盖驾驷、鼓车、安车、驸马骑、玉具刀剑、什物，给彩布二千匹。

translations.literal: Granted green canopy harness four—drum cart—peace cart—side-horse riders—jade-fitted sword blade—misc goods—supply colored cloth two thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: He received green-canopied carriages, drum and riding carts, escort horse, jade-hilt blades, sundries, and two thousand bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 赐单于阏氏以下金锦错杂具，軿车马二乘。

translations.literal: Granted Chanyu Yan-zhi downward gold brocade mixed assorted goods—screened carriage horses two teams.
translations.idiomatic: The queen and household received gold brocade and goods; two screened carriages were granted.

sentences.zh: 遣行中郎将持节护送单于归南庭。

translations.literal: Dispatched acting Commandant hold insignia escort protect Chanyu return Southern Court.
translations.idiomatic: An acting colonel with insignia escorted him to the southern court.

sentences.zh: 诏太常、大鸿胪与诸国侍子于广阳城门外祖会，飨赐作乐，角抵百戏。

translations.literal: Edict Grand Master of Ceremonies, Grand Herald with various states attendant sons at Guangyang city gate outside farewell meeting—feast grant make music—horn butt hundred entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Master of Ceremonies and Grand Herald gave the hostage sons a farewell feast outside Guangyang gate with music and acrobats.

sentences.zh: 顺帝幸胡桃宫临观之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shun favored Walnut Palace arrived watched it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun watched from Walnut Palace.

sentences.zh: 冬，中郎将马寔募刺杀句龙吾斯，送首洛阳。

translations.literal: Winter—Commandant Ma Shi recruited assassinate Goulong Wusi—sent head Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Winter: Colonel Ma Shi had Wusi assassinated and sent his head to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 建康元年，进击余党，斩首千二百级。

translations.literal: Jiankang first year—advanced struck remainder faction—beheaded heads one thousand two hundred grades.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang 1 (144 CE): follow-up strikes took twelve hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 乌桓七十万余口皆诣寔降，车重、牛、羊，不可胜数。

translations.literal: Wuhuan seventy ten-thousand-plus mouths all went Shi surrender—cart heavy cattle sheep—not able fully count.
translations.idiomatic: Over seven hundred thousand Wuhuan submitted to Ma Shi with baggage trains and herds beyond count.

sentences.zh: 单于兜楼储立五年薨。

translations.literal: Chanyu Dou Louchu, having ruled five years, died.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Louchu ruled five years and died.

sentences.zh: 伊陵尸逐就单于居车兒，建和元年立。

translations.literal: Yilingshizhujiu Chanyu Ju Che’er—Jianhe first year enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Yilingshizhujiu Chanyu Ju Che’er was enthroned in Jianhe 1 (147 CE).

sentences.zh: 至永寿元年，匈奴左薁鞬台耆、且渠伯德等复畔，寇抄美稷、安定，属国都尉张奂击破降之。

translations.literal: At Yishou first year—Xiongnu Left Yujian Taiqi, Juqu Bode et al. again rebel—raid plunder Meiji, Anding—dependent state Commandant Zhang Huan struck broke surrendered them.
translations.idiomatic: By Yishou 1 (155 CE) Taiqi and Bode revolted again, raiding Meiji and Anding; dependent-state commandant Zhang Huan broke and accepted their surrender.

sentences.zh: 事已具《奂传》。

translations.literal: Affairs already fully contained in ‘Zhang Huan biography’.
translations.idiomatic: See Zhang Huan’s biography.

sentences.zh: 延熹元年，南单于诸部并畔，遂与乌桓、鲜卑寇缘边九郡，以张奂为北中郎将讨之，单于诸部悉降。

translations.literal: Yanxi first year—Southern Chanyu various divisions together rebel—thereupon with Wuhuan, Xianbei raid along-border nine commanderies—using Zhang Huan as North Commandant campaign them—Chanyu various divisions all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi 1 (158 CE): the southern tribes rose with Wuhuan and Xianbei against nine frontier commanderies; North Commandant Zhang Huan brought every division to surrender.

sentences.zh: 奂以单于不能统理国事，乃拘之，上立左谷蠡王。

translations.literal: Huan because Chanyu not able unify manage state affairs—thereupon detained him—memorialized establish Left Guyuli King.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huan jailed the Chanyu for failing his realm and asked to install the Left Guyuli king.

sentences.zh: 桓帝诏曰：“《春秋》大居正，居车皃一心向化，何罪而黜！

translations.literal: Emperor Huan edict said: “‘Spring and Autumn’ great dwell correct—Ju Chemian singly heart toward transformation—what guilt yet dismiss!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huan replied: ‘The Spring and Autumn honors rightful rule—Ju Chemian is loyal—what crime warrants deposition?’

sentences.zh: 其遣还庭。

translations.literal: Order dispatch return court.
translations.idiomatic: Send him back to his court.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark of Emperor Huan’s edict.
translations.idiomatic: End of the edict.

sentences.zh: 单于居车皃立二十五年薨，子某立。

translations.literal: Chanyu Ju Chemian, having ruled twenty-five years, died—son Mou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Chemian ruled twenty-five years and died; his son (name omitted) succeeded.

sentences.zh: 屠特若尸逐就单于某，熹平元年立。

translations.literal: Teruoruoshizhujiu Chanyu Mou—Xiping first year enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Teruoruoshizhujiu Chanyu [name omitted] took the throne in Xiping 1 (172 CE).

sentences.zh: 六年，单于与中郎将臧旻出雁门击鲜卑檀石槐，大败而还。

translations.literal: Sixth year—Chanyu with Commandant Zang Min exited Yanmen strike Xianbei Tanshi Huai—great defeat and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he joined Colonel Zang Min through Yanmen against Tanshi Huai’s Xianbei and suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 是岁，单于薨，子呼徵立。

translations.literal: This year—Chanyu died—son Huzhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Chanyu died; his son Huzhi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 单于呼徵，光和元年立。

translations.literal: Chanyu Huzhi—Guanghe first year enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Chanyu Huzhi was enthroned in Guanghe 1 (178 CE).

sentences.zh: 二年，中郎将张脩与单于不相能，脩擅斩之，更立右贤王羌渠为单于。

translations.literal: Second year—Commandant Zhang Xiu with Chanyu not mutually able—Xiu on own authority beheaded him—anew established Right Wise King Qiangqu as Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 Colonel Zhang Xiu fell out with the Chanyu, executed him without orders, and set up Right Wise King Qiangqu.

sentences.zh: 脩以不先请而擅诛杀，槛车征诣廷尉抵罪。

translations.literal: Xiu because not first ask yet on own authority execute kill—cage cart summoned arrive Commandant of Justice answer guilt.
translations.idiomatic: For killing without prior approval he was hauled in a prison cart to the Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 单于羌渠，光和二年立。

translations.literal: Chanyu Qiangqu—Guanghe second year enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Chanyu Qiangqu was enthroned in Guanghe 2 (179 CE).

sentences.zh: 中平四年，前中山太守张纯反畔，遂率鲜卑寇边郡。

translations.literal: Zhongping fourth year—former Zhongshan prefect Zhang Chun rebel betray—thereupon led Xianbei raid border commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongping 4 (187 CE): ex-prefect Zhang Chun rebelled and led the Xianbei against the frontier.

sentences.zh: 灵帝诏发南匈奴兵，配幽州牧刘虞讨之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling edict mobilize Southern Xiongnu troops—assign Youzhou Shepherd Liu Yu campaign them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling ordered southern Xiongnu troops attached to Youzhou shepherd Liu Yu against them.

sentences.zh: 单于遣左贤王将骑诣幽州。

translations.literal: Chanyu dispatched Left Wise King lead riders go Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu sent the Left Wise King with cavalry to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 国人恐单于发兵无已，五年，右部䤈落与休著各胡白马铜等十余万人反，攻杀单于。

translations.literal: Country people feared Chanyu dispatch troops without cease—fifth year—Right division Xiluo with Xiuzhu various Hu Baimatong et al. over hundred thousand persons rebel—attacked killed Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes feared endless levies; in year 5 over a hundred thousand men of the right-wing Xiluo, Xiuzhu Hu, Baimatong, and others rose up and slew Chanyu Qiangqu.

sentences.zh: 单于羌渠立十年，子右贤王於扶罗立。

translations.literal: Chanyu Qiangqu ruled ten years—son Right Wise King Yufuluo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Qiangqu had ruled ten years; his son Yufuluo, the Right Wise King, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 持至尸逐侯单于於扶罗，中平五年立。

translations.literal: Chizhishizhuhou Chanyu Yufuluo—Zhongping fifth year enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Chizhishizhuhou Chanyu Yufuluo was enthroned in Zhongping 5 (188 CE).

sentences.zh: 国人杀其父者遂畔，共立须卜骨都侯为单于，而於扶罗诣阙自讼。

translations.literal: Country people who killed his father then rebelled—together established Xubu Gudu Marquis as Chanyu—but Yufuluo went palace gate self plead.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had killed his father broke away and set up the Xubu Gudu marquis as Chanyu while Yufuluo went to the capital to plead his case.

sentences.zh: 会灵帝崩，天下大乱，单于将数千骑与白波贼合兵寇河内诸郡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ling died—under Heaven great chaos—Chanyu led several thousand riders with White Wave bandits combined troops raid Henei various commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling died and the realm dissolved; the Chanyu joined thousands of horse to the White Wave rebels and raided Henei.

sentences.zh: 时民皆保聚，抄掠无利，而兵遂挫伤。

translations.literal: At time people all fortified gathered—raid plunder no profit—and troops then thwarted injured.
translations.idiomatic: The people had walled up; raiding brought no gain and his force wasted away.

sentences.zh: 复欲归国，国人不受，乃止河东。

translations.literal: Again wished return state—country people did not accept—thereupon stopped Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to go home but his people refused him, so he halted east of the river.

sentences.zh: 须卜骨都侯为单于一年而死，南庭遂虚其位，以老王行国事。

translations.literal: Xubu Gudu Marquis as Chanyu one year then died—Southern Court then emptied its seat—using old king conduct state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Xubu Gudu marquis ruled one year and died; the southern court left the throne empty while an elder king handled affairs.

sentences.zh: 单于於扶罗立七年死，弟呼厨泉立。

translations.literal: Chanyu Yufuluo ruled seven years died—younger brother Huchuquan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yufuluo ruled seven years and died; his brother Huchuquan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 论曰：“汉初遭冒顿凶黠，种众强炽。

translations.literal: Discussion says: “Han beginning encountered Modu fierce crafty—seed crowds strong blazing.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary runs: At Han’s rise Modu was ruthless and his tribes strong.

sentences.zh: 高祖威加四海，而窘平城之围。

translations.literal: Gaozu awe extended four seas—yet distressed Pingcheng’s siege.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu awed the realm yet was trapped at Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 太宗政邻刑措，不雪愤辱之耻。

translations.literal: Taizong governance neighbor punishments set aside—not wiped resentful shame’s disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen’s realm knew peace yet never avenged the affront.

sentences.zh: 逮孝武亟兴边略，有志匈奴，赫然命将，戎旗星属，候列郊甸，火通甘泉，而犹鸣镝扬尘，出入畿内，至于穷竭武力，单用天财，历纪岁以攘之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu urgently raised border strategy—had ambition Xiongnu—brilliantly ordered generals—war banners star-linked—watch posts arrayed suburban fields—signal fires reached Ganquan—yet still whistling arrows raised dust—entered exited capital region—as for exhausting military force—only used Heaven’s wealth—passed years ages to expel them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu mobilized the frontier: banners crowded like stars, beacons ran to Ganquan—yet whistling arrows still stirred dust inside the capital belt; he poured armies and treasury into decades of war.

sentences.zh: 寇虽颇折，而汉之疲耗略相当矣。

translations.literal: Raiders although somewhat broken—but Han’s exhaustion waste roughly matched.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians bent but Han’s exhaustion matched their losses.

sentences.zh: 宣帝值虏庭分争，呼韩邪来臣，乃权纳怀柔，因为边卫，罢关徼之儆，息兵民之劳。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan encountered enemy court divide contend—Huhanye came minister—thereupon expedient admit gentle soothe—thereby became border guard—ceased pass lookout alert—rested troops people’s toil.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern court split, Huhanye submitted; Xuan soothed him into a frontier shield—alarms on the passes ceased and soldier and farmer rested.

sentences.zh: 龙驾帝服，鸣钟传鼓于清渭之上，南面而朝单于，朔、易无复匹马之踪，六十余年矣。

translations.literal: Dragon chariot emperor robes—ring bell transmit drum on clear Wei above—south face while court Chanyu—Shuo, Yi no again single horse’s trace—sixty-plus years.
translations.idiomatic: With imperial carriages on the clear Wei, bells and drums rolling, the emperor faced south while the Chanyu attended court—sixty years without a northern horse near Shuoyi.

sentences.zh: 后王莽陵篡，犹动戎夷，续以更始之乱，方夏幅裂。

translations.literal: After Wang Mang overbearing usurp—still stirred Rong Yi—continued with Gengshi’s chaos—fang Xia bolt-split torn.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang’s usurpation stirred the tribes; Gengshi’s turmoil shattered the realm.

sentences.zh: 自是匈奴得志，狼心复生，乘间侵佚，害流傍境。

translations.literal: From this Xiongnu obtained ambition—wolf heart again born—seize gap invade idle—harm flowed neighboring borders.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Xiongnu tasted victory; wolfish hunger returned and raids spilled onto every march.

sentences.zh: 及中兴之初，更通旧好，报命连属，金币载道，而单于骄踞益横，内暴滋深。

translations.literal: When revival beginning—again connect old friendship—return missions continuous—gold coins filled roads—but Chanyu arrogant perch ever crosswise—internal violence grew deep.
translations.idiomatic: Early Guangwu reopened ties—envoys and gold clogged the roads—yet the Chanyu grew arrogant and brutal within.

sentences.zh: 世祖以用事诸华，未遑沙塞之外，忍愧思难，徒报谢而已。

translations.literal: Shizu because managing affairs various Hua—not leisure desert beyond—endure shame think hardship—only return thanks only.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu was busy within China and could not ride north—he swallowed shame and answered with civility.

sentences.zh: 因徒幽、并之民，增边屯之卒。

translations.literal: Thereby shifted You, Bing’s people—increase border station troops.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled You and Bing folk and thickened frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 及关东稍定，陇、蜀已清，其猛夫扞将，莫不顿足攘手，争言卫、霍之事。

translations.literal: When east of passes gradually settled—Long, Shu already cleared—those fierce men shielding generals—none not stamp foot rub hands—contend speak Wei, Huo’s affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once the east settled and Long and Shu were pacified, every bold general stamped and cried for another Wei Qing or Huo Qubing.

sentences.zh: 帝方厌兵，闲修文政，未之许也。

translations.literal: Emperor just weary troops—leisurely cultivate civil administration—not it permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted peace and letters, not war—he refused.

sentences.zh: 其后匈奴争立，日逐来奔，愿修呼韩之好，以御北狄之中，奉籓称臣，永为外扞。

translations.literal: Afterward Xiongnu contended rule—Rizhu came flee—wished restore Huhanye’s friendship—to ward northern Di’s center—present vassal style minister—forever be outer shield.
translations.idiomatic: Then the north split; Rizhu fled south to renew Huhanye’s pact—holding rival factions of the northern tribes in check as a titled vassal.

sentences.zh: 天子总揽群策，和而纳焉。

translations.literal: Son of Heaven gathered all strategies—harmonized and admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: The throne weighed counsel and accepted him in peace.

sentences.zh: 乃诏有司，开北鄙，择肥美之地，量水草以处之。

translations.literal: Thereupon edict responsible offices—open north border—choose fertile beautiful lands—measure water grass to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Officers opened the northern march, chose rich pasture, and quartered them by grass and water.

sentences.zh: 驰中郎之使，尽法度以临之。

translations.literal: Gallop Commandant’s envoys—exhaust laws regulations to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: Colonels rode circuit with full statute to govern them.

sentences.zh: 制衣裳，备文物，加玺绂之绶，正单于之名。

translations.literal: Regulate robes coats—prepare civil objects—add seal-cord’s ribbons—correct Chanyu’s name.
translations.idiomatic: Robes, regalia, seal-ribbons fixed his title as Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 于是匈奴分破，始有南北二庭焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xiongnu divided broken—first had south north two courts therein.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu split—there were now southern and northern courts.

sentences.zh: 仇衅既深，互同便隙，控弦抗戈，觇望风尘，云屯鸟散，更相驰突，至于陷溃创伤者，靡岁或宁，而汉之塞地晏然矣。

translations.literal: Feud rift already deep—mutually same convenient cracks—draw bow oppose spear—spy watch wind dust—cloud mass bird scatter—mutually gallop strike—as for trap defeat wound injury ones—no year perhaps peaceful—but Han’s barrier lands tranquil indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Malice ran deep; they seized every opening—bows against spears, scouts on the wind—now massed, now scattered, charging each other year on year—yet Han’s wall stayed quiet.

sentences.zh: 后亦颇为出师，并兵穷讨，命窦宪、耿夔之徒，前后并进，皆用果谲，设奇数，异道同会，究掩其窟穴，蹑北追奔三千余里，遂破龙祠，焚罽幕，坑十角，梏阏氏，铭功封石，倡呼而还。

translations.literal: After also somewhat raised troops—combine troops exhaust campaign—ordered Dou Xian, Geng Kui class—front rear together advance—all used decisive deceit—set odd stratagems—different routes same meet—ultimately surprise their den holes—track north pursue flee three thousand-plus li—thereupon broke dragon sacrifice—burned felt tents—pit ten horns—cuffed Yan-zhi—inscribe merit seal stone—chant shout and return.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han sent Dou Xian and Geng Kui by ruse and converging columns—surprising their dens, chasing three thousand li past dragon rites—burning felts, slaughtering stock, shackling the queen—carving stone odes—then chanting victory home.

sentences.zh: 单于震慑，屏气蒙氈，遁走于乌孙之地，而漠北空矣。

translations.literal: Chanyu shocked terrified—hold breath cover felt—fled escape at Wusun’s lands—and desert north emptied.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu fled breathless into Wusun country—the northern desert stood empty.

sentences.zh: 若因其时势，及其虚旷，还南虏于阴山，归西河干内地，上申光武权宜之略，下防戎羯乱华之变，使耿国之算不谬于当世，袁安之议见从于后王，平易正直，若此其弘也。

translations.literal: If riding their season momentum—reach their empty vast—return southern captives to Yin mountains—return Xihe dry interior lands—above extend Guangwu expedient strategy—below guard Rong Jie disorder Hua’s changes—make Geng Guo’s reckoning not wrong in present generation—Yuan An’s deliberation seen followed at later kings—level easy upright straight—like this its greatness.
translations.idiomatic: Had Han used that opening—reset the south on the Yinshan and Xihe inland—honoring Guangwu’s expedient and Yuan An’s caution—the policy would have been vast and sound.

sentences.zh: 而窦宪矜三捷之效，忽经世之规，狼戾不端，专行威惠。

translations.literal: But Dou Xian boasted three victories’ effect—neglected governing-age’s norms—wolf-brutal not upright—solely practiced awe grace.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Xian preened over three victories, ignored statecraft, acted wolfishly, and played tyrant and patron alone.

sentences.zh: 遂复更立北虏，反其故庭，并恩两护，以私己福，弃蔑天公，坐树大鲠。

translations.literal: Thereupon again anew established Northern captive—returned their old court—together favor two protections—for private self fortune—discard despise Heaven’s justice—sit plant great obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a northern puppet in its old seat, pampered two shields for private gain, defied principle, and planted lasting trouble.

sentences.zh: 永言前载，何恨愤之深乎！

translations.literal: Long speak former records—what resent rage’s depth!
translations.idiomatic: Reading that past—what bitterness!

sentences.zh: 自后经纶失方，畔服不一，其为疢毒，胡可单言！

translations.literal: Afterward weave-plan lose direction—rebel submit not one—its become scorch poison—how can singly speak!
translations.idiomatic: Later strategy failed—now rebel, now submit—poison beyond words!

sentences.zh: 降及后世，玩为常俗，终于吞噬神乡，丘墟帝宅。

translations.literal: Down to later generations—trifle as constant custom—finally reach swallow divine homeland—mound ruin emperor dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages treated it lightly until the holy heartland was devoured and the throne lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 呜呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 千里之差，兴自毫端，失得之源，百世不磨矣。

translations.literal: Thousand li’s difference—rises from hair tip—lose gain’s source—hundred generations not grind away.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand-li error begins at a hair’s breadth—gain and loss echo forever.

sentences.zh: 赞曰：匈奴既分，羽书稀闻。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Xiongnu already divided—feather dispatch rarely heard.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict: once the Xiongnu split, urgent bulletins grew rare.

sentences.zh: 野心难悔，终亦纷纭。

translations.literal: Wild heart hard repent—end also numerous confused.
translations.idiomatic: Their wild hearts never repented—turmoil to the end.
